questions.q: We should never share our ______ with strangers online.
questions.e: A password is secret. We must never share it with strangers.

questions.q: If someone online makes you feel scared, tell your ______ or teacher.
questions.e: Always tell parents or a teacher if anything online scares you.

questions.q: Young children should use the internet only with an ______ nearby.
questions.e: An adult can help keep us safe on the internet.

questions.q: A pop-up says 'You won a prize! Click here'. We should ______ it.
questions.e: Such pop-ups can be tricks. We should close or ignore them.

questions.q: A stranger in an online game asks Arjun some questions. Answer yes or no.
p: (a) Should Arjun tell the stranger his school name?
no
(b) Should he agree to meet the stranger?
no
(c) Should he tell his parents about it?
yes
questions.e: Never share personal details or meet online strangers, and always tell parents.

questions.q: A computer works very fast. This feature is called ______.
questions.e: Speed means a computer can do a lot of work in a very short time.

questions.q: A computer gives correct results every time. This feature is called ______.
questions.e: Accuracy means a computer does not make mistakes if the instructions are correct.

questions.q: A computer can work for hours without getting tired or bored. This feature is called ______.
questions.e: Diligence means a computer works for long hours with the same care.

questions.q: A computer can do many different kinds of work, like drawing, typing and playing music. This feature is called ______.
questions.e: Versatility means a computer can do many different types of jobs.

questions.q: Riya keeps 5000 photos, 300 songs and many stories on her computer. Which feature of a computer helps her do this?
questions.e: A computer has a large storage capacity, so it can keep a huge amount of data.

questions.q: CPU stands for Central ______ Unit.
questions.e: CPU means Central Processing Unit, the brain of the computer.

questions.q: The three parts of the CPU are the ALU, the CU and the ______ Unit.
questions.e: The CPU has the Arithmetic Logic Unit, the Control Unit and the Memory Unit.

questions.q: ALU stands for Arithmetic and ______ Unit.
questions.e: The Arithmetic and Logic Unit does sums and compares numbers.

questions.q: Which part of the CPU controls and guides all the work of the computer?
questions.e: The Control Unit (CU) controls all the parts of the computer, like a traffic police officer.

questions.q: Devices used to give data or instructions to a computer are called ______ devices.
questions.e: Input devices, like the keyboard and mouse, send data into the computer.

questions.q: Devices that show or give us the result are called ______ devices.
questions.e: Output devices, like the monitor and printer, give us the result.

questions.q: A keyboard is an ______ device.
questions.e: We give instructions through the keyboard, so it is an input device.

questions.q: A printer is an ______ device.
questions.e: A printer gives the result on paper, so it is an output device.

questions.q: A ______ copies a picture from paper into the computer. It is an input device.
questions.e: A scanner reads a paper picture or page and sends it into the computer.

questions.q: A ______ is an input device used to record our voice.
questions.e: A microphone takes in sound, so it is an input device.

questions.q: Riya records a song on the computer and listens to it.
p: (a) Name one output device she can use to listen to the song.
speakers|speaker|headphones|headphone|earphones|earphone
(b) A touch screen takes our touch and also shows pictures. Is it used for input, output or both?
both|input and output
(c) Which input device with a stick is used to play racing games?
joystick|joy stick
questions.e: Speakers and headphones are output devices; a touch screen is both input and output; a joystick is an input device for games.

questions.q: We can send messages in a few seconds using ______.
questions.e: Email (electronic mail) sends messages through the internet in seconds.

questions.q: Online ______ lets us buy things from home using a computer.
questions.e: In online shopping we choose and order things on the internet.

questions.q: Scientists use computers to predict the ______ for the coming days.
questions.e: Weather forecasts are made using computers and satellite pictures.

questions.q: Computers at ISRO help to launch and control ______.
questions.e: ISRO uses computers to launch rockets and control satellites in space.

questions.q: The ______ key moves the cursor forward by a few spaces at once.
questions.e: Pressing Tab moves the cursor a fixed number of spaces ahead.

questions.q: Keys F1 to F12 are called ______ keys.
questions.e: F1 to F12 are function keys; each does a special job, like F1 for Help.

questions.q: The ______ key is used to cancel or stop a task.
questions.e: The Escape (Esc) key cancels the current task.

questions.q: The keys on the right side of the keyboard that look like a calculator are called the ______ keypad.
questions.e: The numeric keypad helps us type numbers quickly.

questions.q: The Home key takes the cursor to the ______ of the line.
questions.e: Home takes the cursor to the start of the line; End takes it to the end.

questions.q: Arjun typed 'i love Indiaa' and wants to correct it.
p: (a) Which key does he hold down to type a capital 'I'?
Shift
(b) Which key takes the cursor straight to the end of the line?
End
(c) Which key deletes the letter on the right side of the cursor?
Delete|Del
questions.e: Shift with a letter types a capital, End jumps to the end of the line, and Delete removes the letter to the right of the cursor.

questions.q: Moving the pointer over an item without clicking is called ______.
questions.e: When we hover over an item, a small tip often appears.

questions.q: A right click shows a list of choices called a ______ menu.
questions.e: Right-clicking opens a shortcut (context) menu with useful choices.

questions.q: The two kinds of mouse are wired and ______.
questions.e: A wireless mouse has no wire and works with a battery.

questions.q: An ______ mouse uses light to sense how it moves.
questions.e: An optical mouse has a small light under it instead of a ball.

questions.q: Riya wants to select many words at once. She holds the left button and ______ the mouse over the words.
questions.e: Dragging over words with the left button pressed selects all of them.

questions.q: The ______ tool picks up a colour from the picture.
questions.a: Color picker|Colour picker|picker|eyedropper|color picker tool|colour picker tool
questions.e: The Color picker copies a colour from the drawing so we can use it again.

questions.q: The ______ tool makes the picture look bigger so we can see small parts.
questions.e: The Magnifier zooms in on a part of the picture.

questions.q: The ______ group in Paint has ready-made shapes like rectangle, oval and star.
questions.e: The Shapes group lets us draw neat shapes quickly.

questions.q: To choose a part of the picture and move it, we use the ______ tool.
questions.e: The Select tool marks a part of the picture so we can move, copy or cut it.

questions.q: In Paint, Color 1 is the foreground colour and Color 2 is the ______ colour.
questions.e: Color 1 is used for drawing (foreground) and Color 2 for the background.

questions.q: Meera is making a Diwali card in Paint.
p: (a) Which tool will she use to write 'Happy Diwali'?
Text|A|Text tool
(b) Which tool will fill the diya with orange colour?
Fill with Color|Fill with Colour|Fill|bucket|paint bucket|Fill tool
(c) Which tool will remove an extra line?
Eraser|rubber
questions.e: Text writes words, Fill with Color colours a closed area, and Eraser removes unwanted parts.

questions.q: The screen that appears after the computer starts is the ______.
questions.e: The desktop is the main screen with icons and the taskbar.

questions.q: Files we delete go to the ______.
questions.e: Deleted files go to the Recycle Bin, from where they can be brought back.

questions.q: The picture on the desktop background is called the ______.
questions.e: The wallpaper is the picture behind the icons on the desktop.

questions.q: When a computer hangs, we switch it off and on again using one option. This is called ______.
questions.e: Restart closes everything and starts the computer again.

questions.q: Arjun wants to switch off the computer correctly.
p: (a) Which button does he click first?
Start|Start button|Windows
(b) Which option does he finally click to turn off the computer?
Shut down|shutdown
(c) After the computer shuts down, what should he switch off on the wall?
main switch|switch|main power|power supply|plug
questions.e: Click Start, then Power, then Shut down, and finally switch off the main switch.

questions.q: We should use a ______ to keep the computer safe from sudden power cuts and voltage changes.
questions.e: A UPS gives power for some time during a cut, and protects the computer.

questions.q: We should keep the computer room free from ______ and moisture.
questions.e: Dust and moisture can damage the parts of a computer.

questions.q: A program that protects a computer from viruses is called an ______.
questions.e: Antivirus software finds and removes viruses from the computer.

questions.q: A secret word used to open our account is called a ______.
questions.e: A password keeps our account safe; we must keep it secret.

questions.q: We should not open emails or links sent by ______.
questions.e: Messages from strangers may have viruses or tricks.

questions.q: Being mean to or bullying someone online is called ______.
questions.e: Cyberbullying is bullying using phones or the internet. We must report it to an adult.

questions.q: A harmful program that can damage files on a computer is called a ______.
questions.e: A computer virus spreads to other files and can damage them.

questions.q: Riya gets a message: 'Send your home address to win a free cycle!' Answer yes or no.
p: (a) Should she send her home address?
no
(b) Should she tell her parents about the message?
yes
(c) Is it safe to share our password with friends?
no
questions.e: Never share personal details or passwords online, and always tell parents about such messages.

questions.q: The physical parts of a computer that we can see and touch are called ______.
questions.e: Hardware means the physical parts like the monitor, keyboard and CPU that we can touch.

questions.q: A set of programs that tells the computer what to do is called ______.
questions.e: Software is a set of instructions (programs); we cannot touch it, but it makes the hardware work.

questions.q: Which input device is used to type letters and numbers into a computer?
questions.e: The keyboard has keys for letters, numbers and symbols, so it is used for typing.

questions.q: Which output device shows text and pictures on a screen?
questions.e: The monitor (Visual Display Unit) displays the output on a screen.

questions.q: The smallest unit of computer memory is a ______.
questions.e: A bit (binary digit) is either 0 or 1 and is the smallest unit of memory.

questions.q: A small portable storage device that is plugged into a USB port is called a ______ drive.
questions.e: A pen drive (USB flash drive) is small, portable and connects through a USB port.

questions.q: Windows is an example of an ______ system.
questions.e: Windows is an operating system; it manages the computer and lets us run other programs.

questions.q: MS Word is a ______ processing software used to type letters and stories.
questions.e: MS Word is a word processor used to type, edit and format text documents.

questions.q: Which tool in MS Paint is used to fill a closed shape with colour?
questions.a: fill with color|fill with colour|fill|paint bucket|bucket
questions.e: The Fill with colour tool (paint bucket) fills a closed area with the selected colour.

questions.q: A worldwide network of computers connected to each other is called the ______.
questions.e: The Internet is a huge network that connects computers all over the world.

questions.q: A secret word used to protect your account or computer is called a ______.
questions.e: A password keeps your account safe; it should never be shared with strangers.

questions.q: The character that moves and acts on the stage in Scratch is called a ______.
questions.e: A sprite is an object or character in Scratch, like the orange cat, that follows our scripts.

questions.q: In Scratch, the background picture of the stage is called a ______.
questions.e: A backdrop is the background of the stage; a sprite's different looks are called costumes.

questions.q: Which input device is used to copy a printed photo or page into the computer?
questions.e: A scanner reads a printed page or photo and changes it into a digital image.

questions.q: MS Paint and MS Word are examples of ______ software.
questions.e: Application software helps us do a particular task, such as drawing or typing.

questions.q: Which part of the computer is known as its brain?
questions.e: The CPU (Central Processing Unit) processes all data and instructions, so it is called the brain of the computer.

questions.q: How many bits make one byte?
questions.e: 8 bits = 1 byte. A group of 4 bits is called a nibble.

questions.q: Which memory loses all its data when the computer is switched off?
questions.e: RAM is temporary (volatile) memory; its contents are lost when the power goes off.

questions.q: 1 kilobyte (KB) is equal to how many bytes?
questions.e: In computer memory, 1 KB = 1024 bytes.

questions.q: Output printed on paper is called ______ copy.
questions.e: A printout on paper is a hard copy; output seen on the screen is a soft copy.

questions.q: A container in which files are kept together on a computer is called a ______.
questions.e: Folders help us keep related files together in an organised way.

questions.q: When you delete a file in Windows, it first goes to the ______.
questions.e: Deleted files go to the Recycle Bin, from where they can be restored if needed.

questions.q: Which shortcut key makes the selected text bold in MS Word?
questions.e: Ctrl+B makes text bold, Ctrl+I makes it italic and Ctrl+U underlines it.

questions.q: Which key is pressed in MS Word to start a new paragraph?
questions.e: Pressing Enter moves the cursor to a new line and starts a new paragraph.

questions.q: In MS Paint, which tool is used to pick up a colour from the picture itself?
questions.e: The Colour picker copies a colour from any part of the picture so it can be used again.

questions.q: While drawing with the Oval tool in Paint, which key is held down to get a perfect circle?
questions.e: Holding Shift while dragging the Oval tool draws a perfect circle; with the Rectangle tool it draws a square.

questions.q: A program such as Google Chrome used to open and view websites is called a web ______.
questions.e: A web browser lets us open and view web pages; Chrome, Edge and Firefox are browsers.

questions.q: Which symbol separates the user name and the domain name in an email address such as riya@gmail.com?
questions.e: Every email address has the @ symbol between the user name and the domain name.

questions.q: Sending hurtful or threatening messages to someone online is called cyber ______.
questions.e: Cyberbullying means troubling someone using the internet; it should be reported to a trusted adult.

questions.q: In Scratch, the 'move 10 steps' block is found in which block category?
questions.e: Motion blocks (blue) move and turn a sprite, such as 'move 10 steps' and 'turn 15 degrees'.

questions.q: A sprite is at x = 0 and faces right. It runs 'move 10 steps' inside a 'repeat 5' block. What is its x-position now?
questions.e: The move block runs 5 times: 10 × 5 = 50 steps, so x becomes 50.

questions.q: The block 'when green flag clicked' starts a script. It belongs to which block category?
questions.e: Events blocks (yellow) start scripts, for example when the green flag or a key is clicked.

questions.q: Riya has a 4 GB pen drive. How many MB is that? (1 GB = 1024 MB)
A touch screen on a mobile phone works as both an input device and an ______ device.
questions.e: We give input by touching the screen, and the same screen shows the output.

questions.q: Meera typed the heading 'My Village' and wants it in the middle of the line. Which alignment should she use?
questions.e: Centre alignment places the text in the middle between the left and right margins.

questions.q: Arjun deleted a sentence by mistake. Which shortcut key will bring it back?
questions.e: Ctrl+Z is Undo; it reverses the last action. Ctrl+Y is Redo.

questions.q: Meera wants to give a new name to her folder 'Holi Photos'. Which option should she choose after right-clicking it?
questions.e: The Rename option lets us change the name of a file or folder.

questions.q: An email says 'You have won a prize! Click this link and enter your password.' A fake message like this that tries to steal your details is called ______.
questions.e: Phishing messages pretend to be genuine to steal passwords and personal details; never click such links.

questions.q: Which of these is the strongest password?
questions.e: A strong password is long and mixes capital and small letters, numbers and special symbols.

questions.q: An email that you have written but not yet sent is saved in the ______ folder.
questions.e: Unsent emails are kept in Drafts so that you can finish and send them later.

questions.q: In Paint, Meera wants her drawing to look bigger on the screen only, without changing the actual drawing. Which tool should she use?
questions.e: The Magnifier (zoom) only changes how big the picture looks on screen; Resize changes the actual picture.

questions.q: CDs and DVDs, which are read using a laser beam, are ______ storage devices.
questions.e: CDs and DVDs are optical discs because data on them is read and written with a laser.

questions.q: Arjun types a story on his computer, prints it and then listens to music.
p: (a) Which device does he use to type the story?
keyboard|key board
(b) Which device gives him the story on paper?
printer
(c) Which output device lets him hear the music?
speaker|speakers|headphones|headphone|earphones
questions.e: The keyboard is an input device, while the printer and speakers are output devices.

questions.q: Meera's computer has 8 GB RAM and a 512 GB hard disk.
p: (a) Which of the two is the primary (main) memory?
RAM|random access memory
(b) Which of the two keeps her files saved even after the computer is switched off?
hard disk|hard disc|HDD|hard drive|hard disk drive
(c) How many MB is 8 GB? (1 GB = 1024 MB)
MB
questions.e: RAM is temporary primary memory, while the hard disk is permanent secondary storage; 8 × 1024 = 8192 MB.

questions.q: A sprite with pen down runs this script: when green flag clicked, repeat 4 [move 100 steps, turn right 90 degrees].
p: (a) Which shape does the sprite draw?
square|a square
(b) How many steps does it move in all?
steps
(c) How many degrees does it turn in all?
degrees
questions.e: Four equal sides with four 90° turns make a square: 4 × 100 = 400 steps and 4 × 90 = 360 degrees.

questions.q: Riya is writing an email to her teacher at teacher@school.in and wants to send a copy to her mother too.
p: (a) In which box should she type her teacher's email address?
To
(b) In which box should she type her mother's address to send a copy?
CC|carbon copy
(c) What is the domain name in teacher@school.in?
school.in|schoolin|school in
questions.e: The main receiver goes in To, a copy goes in CC, and the part after @ is the domain name.

questions.q: Arjun is typing a paragraph on 'My India' in MS Word.
p: (a) Which shortcut key makes the selected text italic?
Ctrl+I|Ctrl I|CtrlI|Control+I|Control I
(b) Which key deletes the character to the left of the cursor?
Backspace|back space
(c) Which shortcut key saves the document?
Ctrl+S|Ctrl S|CtrlS|Control+S|Control S
questions.e: Ctrl+I gives italics and Ctrl+S saves; Backspace removes the character to the left while Delete removes the one to the right.

questions.q: Meera saved her drawing as a file named diwali.bmp.
p: (a) What is the extension of this file?
bmp|.bmp
(b) Which program did she most likely use to make it?
Paint|MS Paint|Microsoft Paint
(c) Which key on the keyboard deletes a selected file?
Delete|Del|delete key
questions.e: The part after the dot is the extension; .bmp is the default bitmap picture format of Paint.

questions.q: In Scratch, a sprite starts at x = -100. It runs 'change x by 20' inside a 'repeat 10' block. What is its final x-position?
questions.e: It changes x by 20 ten times, i.e. by 200 in all: -100 + 200 = 100.

questions.q: While playing an online game, a stranger asks Riya to meet him alone. What is the safest thing for her to do?
questions.a: Not reply and tell a parent or teacher
questions.e: Never meet or share details with online strangers; always tell a trusted adult such as a parent or teacher.

questions.q: The first screen we see after Windows starts is called the ______.
questions.e: The desktop is the main screen of Windows, with icons, the taskbar and the Start button.

questions.q: The bar at the bottom of the Windows screen that shows the Start button and open programs is called the ______.
questions.e: The taskbar shows the Start button, open programs, the clock and other icons.

questions.q: Each page of a PowerPoint presentation is called a ______.
questions.e: A presentation is made of slides that are shown one after another.

questions.q: A PowerPoint 2007 (or later) presentation is saved with the extension ______.
questions.e: PowerPoint files use .pptx, Word files use .docx and Excel files use .xlsx.

questions.q: Software that manages the computer and helps other programs to run is called ______ software.
questions.e: System software, such as an operating system, controls the computer; application software does specific tasks.

questions.q: 1 megabyte (MB) is equal to how many kilobytes (KB)?
Which memory stores the start-up instructions permanently and can only be read, not changed?
questions.e: ROM (Read Only Memory) is permanent; its contents are not lost when the computer is switched off.

questions.q: Which input device is used to record our voice into the computer?
questions.e: A microphone takes sound as input; a speaker gives sound as output.

questions.q: Which input device reads the black and white lines printed on products in shops?
questions.a: barcode reader|barcode scanner|bar code reader|bar code scanner|barcode
questions.e: A barcode reader scans the barcode lines and sends the product details to the computer.

questions.q: In MS Word, a grid made of rows and columns is called a ______.
questions.e: A table arranges information in rows and columns; each box is called a cell.

questions.q: The address of a website, such as www.ncert.nic.in, is called a ______.
questions.e: A URL (Uniform Resource Locator) is the unique address of a web page.

questions.q: The emails that you receive are stored in the ______.
questions.e: The Inbox stores received mail; sent mail goes to Sent Items.

questions.q: A harmful program that can damage files and spread from one computer to another is called a computer ______.
questions.e: A computer virus is a harmful program that can delete or damage data and spread to other computers.

questions.q: In Scratch, the area where we drag and join blocks to make a program is called the ______ area.
questions.e: Blocks are joined in the Code (Scripts) area; the result is seen on the stage.

questions.q: MS Word and MS PowerPoint are examples of ______ software.
questions.e: Application software helps users do particular tasks such as typing documents or making presentations.

questions.q: Which part of the CPU does calculations and comparisons?
questions.a: ALU|arithmetic logic unit|arithmetic and logic unit
questions.e: The ALU does arithmetic and logical work, the CU controls all operations, and the memory unit stores data.

questions.q: How many gigabytes (GB) make 1 terabyte (TB)?
A hard disk is an example of ______ memory.
questions.e: Secondary memory like the hard disk stores data permanently; RAM and ROM are primary memory.

questions.q: Which output device is used to print large drawings such as maps and building plans?
questions.e: A plotter prints large, accurate drawings like maps, charts and building designs.

questions.q: A webcam used in an online class is an ______ device.
questions.e: A webcam captures pictures and video and sends them into the computer, so it is an input device.

questions.q: To select many files one by one in Windows, we hold down the ______ key and click each file.
questions.e: Holding Ctrl while clicking selects several files that are not next to each other.

questions.q: Which shortcut key copies the selected file or text?
questions.e: Ctrl+C copies, Ctrl+X cuts and Ctrl+V pastes.

questions.q: Which feature of MS Word is used to change a word into another word everywhere in the document?
questions.e: Find and Replace (Ctrl+H) finds a word and replaces it with another throughout the document.

questions.q: Text that appears at the top of every page of a Word document is called the ______.
questions.e: The header appears at the top of every page and the footer at the bottom.

questions.q: The special effects seen when one slide changes to the next are called slide ______.
questions.e: Transitions are applied between slides; animations are applied to objects on a slide.

questions.q: Which key starts the slide show from the first slide in PowerPoint?
questions.e: F5 starts the slide show from the beginning; Shift+F5 starts it from the current slide.

questions.q: A website such as Google that helps us find information on the internet is called a ______.
questions.e: A search engine searches the web for the words we type; a browser is the program used to open websites.

questions.q: Which box in an email is used to send a copy secretly, so that other receivers do not see that address?
questions.e: Addresses in BCC (Blind Carbon Copy) are hidden from the other receivers.

questions.q: Copying someone else's work from the internet and showing it as your own is called ______.
questions.e: Plagiarism is unfair; we should always give credit to the source we use.

questions.q: In Scratch, the 'repeat' and 'forever' blocks are found in which block category?
questions.e: Control blocks (orange) include repeat, forever, wait and if-then.

questions.q: A sprite runs 'turn 15 degrees' inside a 'repeat 12' block. How many degrees does it turn in all?
questions.e: 15 × 12 = 180 degrees.

questions.q: In Scratch, a variable 'score' is set to 0. Then 'change score by 3' runs inside 'repeat 5'. What is the final value of score?
questions.e: The score increases by 3 five times: 0 + 3 × 5 = 15.

questions.q: In a flowchart, which shape is used to show a decision with Yes/No answers?
questions.e: A diamond shows a decision, a rectangle shows a process, a parallelogram shows input/output and an oval shows start/stop.

questions.q: Each song is 4 MB in size. How many such songs can be stored in a 1 GB pen drive? (1 GB = 1024 MB)
Ravi's project file is 3072 KB in size. What is its size in MB?
Meera wants the words 'Republic Day' to appear in red letters. Which option on the Home tab should she use?
questions.e: Font Colour changes the colour of the letters; Highlight only colours the background behind the text.

questions.q: Arjun inserts a table with 4 rows and 5 columns. How many cells does the table have?
questions.e: Number of cells = rows × columns = 4 × 5 = 20.

questions.q: Riya wants a picture of a bird to fly into her slide during the show. Which tab should she use to add this effect to the picture?
questions.e: Effects on objects within a slide are added from the Animations tab.

questions.q: Arjun selects a file on the desktop and presses Ctrl+X. He then opens a folder. Which shortcut should he press to move the file there?
questions.e: Cut (Ctrl+X) followed by Paste (Ctrl+V) moves a file to a new place.

questions.q: In the web address https://www.ncert.nic.in, which part shows that the website belongs to India?
questions.e: .in is the country code domain for India.

questions.q: A pop-up suddenly says 'Your computer has a virus! Click here to fix it.' What is the safest action?
questions.a: Close it without clicking the link
questions.e: Such pop-ups are often tricks to spread malware; close them and use a trusted antivirus instead.

questions.q: Which device, used in ATMs and smartphones, works as both an input and an output device?
questions.e: A touch screen takes input when touched and also displays the output.

questions.q: A computer has 4 GB RAM, a 1 TB hard disk, and Meera uses a 16 GB pen drive with it.
p: (a) Which of these is primary memory?
RAM|random access memory
(b) What is the size of the pen drive in MB? (1 GB = 1024 MB)
MB
(c) Which of the three is a portable storage device?
pen drive|pendrive|USB drive|flash drive|USB flash drive
questions.e: RAM is primary memory; 16 × 1024 = 16384 MB; a pen drive can be carried from one computer to another.

questions.q: A Scratch script: when green flag clicked, set x to 0, repeat 3 [change x by 10, wait 1 seconds].
p: (a) What is the final value of x?
(b) About how many seconds does the repeat loop take?
seconds
(c) In which block category is the 'wait 1 seconds' block found?
Control
questions.e: The loop runs 3 times, adding 10 and waiting 1 second each time: x = 30 after about 3 seconds; wait is a Control block.

questions.q: Riya is making a presentation of 8 slides on 'Diwali'.
p: (a) Which view shows all slides as small pictures so that she can rearrange them?
Slide Sorter|slide sorter view|sorter
(b) Which key ends the slide show?
Esc|escape
(c) Which tab does she use to add a picture of diyas to a slide?
Insert
questions.e: Slide Sorter view helps reorder slides, Esc ends the show and pictures are added from the Insert tab.

questions.q: Arjun gets an email from an unknown sender: 'Win a free phone! Send your parents' bank details.'
p: (a) Unwanted bulk emails like this are called ______.
spam|junk|junk mail|spam mail
(b) A fake email that tries to steal personal details is called ______.
phishing
(c) Which software should be kept updated to protect the computer from harmful attachments?
antivirus|anti-virus|anti virus|antivirus software
questions.e: Such mails are spam and phishing attempts; never reply, and keep antivirus software updated.

questions.q: Looking at the top element of a stack without removing it is called ______.
questions.e: PEEK (or TOP) only reads the top element; the stack is not changed.

questions.q: In Python, a stack is usually implemented using a ______.
questions.e: A list is mutable and has append() and pop(), which work at the same end, as a stack needs.

questions.q: Which list method is used to implement the PUSH operation of a stack?
questions.e: append() adds an element at the end of the list, which is treated as the top of the stack.

questions.q: In postfix notation, the operator is written ______ its operands.
questions.e: For example, A + B in infix is written AB+ in postfix.

questions.q: Ordinary expressions such as A + B, with the operator between the operands, are written in ______ notation.
questions.e: Infix places the operator between operands; prefix places it before and postfix after.

questions.q:
What is the output?
S = []
S.append(4)
S.append(9)
S.append(1)
S.pop()
print(S[-1])
questions.e: After the pushes S is [4, 9, 1]; pop() removes 1, so the top element S[-1] is 9.

questions.q: What is the value of the postfix expression 8 2 3 * - ?
questions.e: Push 8, 2, 3; * pops 3 and 2 and pushes 6; - pops 6 and 8 and pushes 8 - 6 = 2.

questions.q: What is the postfix form of the infix expression A + B * C?
questions.e: * has higher precedence than +, so B * C becomes BC*, and then A is added: ABC*+.

questions.q: While checking the brackets in '(a+b))' with a stack, an error is found because the last ')' arrives when the stack is ______.
questions.e: Each '(' is pushed and each ')' pops one; the second ')' finds nothing to pop, so the brackets are unbalanced.

questions.q:
S = []
S.append(3)
S.append(7)
S.append(5)
x = S.pop()
S.append(x * 2)
p: (a) What is the top element of S now?
(b) What is len(S)?
(c) What is S[0]?
questions.e: After the pushes S is [3, 7, 5]; 5 is popped and 10 pushed, giving [3, 7, 10].

questions.q: What is the full form of WAN?
questions.e: A WAN connects computers over a large area such as a country or the whole world; the Internet is the largest WAN.

questions.q: Which device converts digital signals to analog signals and back, so that computers can communicate over telephone lines?
questions.e: Modem stands for MOdulator-DEModulator.

questions.q: The first network, started in 1969 by the US Department of Defense, was called ______.
questions.e: ARPANET (Advanced Research Projects Agency Network) linked a few universities and research centres and grew into the Internet.

questions.q: Which protocol is used to transfer files between two computers on a network?
questions.e: FTP (File Transfer Protocol) is used to upload and download files between a client and a server.

questions.q: Which system translates a domain name such as ncert.nic.in into its IP address?
questions.e: DNS servers look up the IP address of a domain name so that the browser can reach the web server.

questions.q: The bandwidth of a communication channel is measured in ______.
questions.e: Bandwidth is the range of frequencies a channel can carry, measured in hertz; data transfer rate is measured in bits per second.

questions.q: Which network device connects two networks that use different protocols?
questions.e: A gateway translates between dissimilar networks and is the entry and exit point of a network.

questions.q: How many bits long is an IPv4 address?
questions.e: An IPv4 address has 32 bits, written as four numbers from 0 to 255 such as 192.168.0.1; IPv6 uses 128 bits.

questions.q: Write the full forms of these networking terms.
p: (a) URL
Uniform Resource Locator
(b) PAN
Personal Area Network
(c) VoIP
Voice over Internet Protocol|Voice over IP
questions.e: A URL is the address of a web resource; a PAN connects personal devices within a few metres; VoIP carries voice calls over the Internet.

questions.q: In DBMS, the letter M stands for ______.
questions.e: DBMS is Database Management System, software used to create and manage databases.

questions.q: In a relational database, a column of a table is called an ______.
questions.e: Columns are attributes (fields); rows are tuples (records).

questions.q: In the relational model, a table is called a ______.
questions.e: A relation is a table of rows (tuples) and columns (attributes).

questions.q: The set of all possible values that an attribute can take is called its ______.
questions.e: For example, the domain of a Gender attribute might be {M, F}.

questions.q: Which key is chosen to uniquely identify each tuple of a relation and cannot contain NULL values?
questions.e: The primary key identifies every row uniquely, so its values must be unique and not NULL.

questions.q: A primary key that is made up of two or more attributes is called a ______ primary key.
questions.e: When no single attribute is unique, a combination such as (RollNo, Section) can be used as a composite key.

questions.q: A table has 6 rows and 3 columns. What is its degree?
questions.e: Degree is the number of attributes (columns), which is 3; the cardinality is 6.

questions.q: Unnecessary repetition of the same data in different files is called data ______.
questions.e: Redundancy wastes storage and can lead to inconsistency; a DBMS reduces it.

questions.q: When copies of the same data in different files do not match after an update, the problem is called data ______.
questions.e: If a change is made in one file but not in another, the data becomes inconsistent.

questions.q: The overall design or structure of a database, which rarely changes, is called the database ______.
questions.e: The schema describes the tables, attributes and constraints; the data stored at a particular moment is an instance.

questions.q: In the relation STUDENT(RollNo, Name, AdmNo, Phone), both RollNo and AdmNo are unique for every student, and RollNo is chosen as the primary key.
p: (a) What is the degree of STUDENT?
(b) What type of key is AdmNo?
alternate|alternate key
(c) What type of keys are RollNo and AdmNo, since either could be the primary key?
candidate|candidate keys|candidate key
questions.e: There are 4 attributes. RollNo and AdmNo are candidate keys; the one not chosen as primary key (AdmNo) is the alternate key.

questions.q: Which SQL command is used to add new rows to a table?
questions.e: INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES (1, 'Amit', 90); adds a new row.

questions.q: Which clause of a SELECT query picks only the rows that satisfy a given condition?
questions.e: SELECT * FROM STUDENT WHERE Marks > 80; returns only the rows with marks above 80.

questions.q: Which keyword is used with SELECT to remove duplicate values from the result?
questions.e: SELECT DISTINCT City FROM STUDENT; shows each city only once.

questions.q: Which SQL command changes the structure of an existing table, for example to add a column?
questions.e: ALTER TABLE STUDENT ADD Phone CHAR(10); adds a new column.

questions.q: Which SQL command changes the data stored in existing rows?
questions.e: UPDATE STUDENT SET Marks = 95 WHERE RollNo = 3; changes the value in matching rows.

questions.q: CREATE, ALTER and DROP belong to which category of SQL commands?
questions.e: DDL commands define or change the structure of database objects; INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE are DML commands.

questions.q: The Marks column has the values 45, 50, 55, 60 and 65. How many rows are returned by SELECT * FROM T WHERE Marks BETWEEN 50 AND 60;?
questions.e: BETWEEN includes both end values, so 50, 55 and 60 are returned.

questions.q: Which condition correctly selects the rows in which the Phone column has no value?
questions.e: NULL cannot be compared with =; the IS NULL operator must be used.

questions.q: The Marks column has the values 10, NULL, 20 and NULL. What does SELECT COUNT(Marks) FROM T; return?
questions.e: COUNT(column) counts only non-NULL values; COUNT(*) would return 4.

questions.q: Which module is imported in the statement import ______ as m to connect a Python program with MySQL?
questions.e: The mysql.connector module provides connect() and the cursor methods used in CBSE programs.

questions.q: Which function of mysql.connector establishes a connection with a MySQL database?
questions.e: con = mysql.connector.connect(host='localhost', user='root', passwd='...', database='school') returns a connection object.

questions.q: Which method of the connection object creates a cursor object?
questions.e: cur = con.cursor() creates a cursor, which is used to run queries and fetch results.

questions.q: Which method is called on the connection object to end the connection with the database?
questions.e: con.close() closes the connection once the work is over.

questions.q: Which method of the connection object returns True if the connection to MySQL was made successfully?
questions.e: if con.is_connected(): print("Connected") is commonly used to check the connection.

questions.q: What does fetchone() return when there are no more rows left to fetch?
questions.e: fetchone() returns the next row as a tuple, or None when the result set is exhausted.

questions.q: fetchall() returns the rows of a result as a ______ of tuples.
questions.e: Each row is a tuple, and fetchall() returns all remaining rows together in a list.

questions.q: Which cursor method fetches a given number of rows, for example 3 rows at a time?
questions.e: cur.fetchmany(3) returns the next 3 rows as a list of tuples.

questions.q: In which Python data type is a single row returned by fetchone()?
questions.e: A row such as (1, 'Amit', 90) is returned as a tuple.

questions.q: In connect(), which parameter gives the name of the database to be used?
questions.e: database='school' selects the school database; host, user and passwd identify the server and the login.

questions.q: The table STUDENT has only 2 rows. After cur.execute("SELECT * FROM STUDENT"), what is the output of print(len(cur.fetchmany(3)))?
questions.e: fetchmany(3) returns at most 3 rows; only 2 rows exist, so the list has 2 tuples.

questions.q: In q = "SELECT * FROM emp WHERE sal > {}".format(5000), which string method puts the value into the query?
questions.e: format() replaces {} with 5000, giving the query string SELECT * FROM emp WHERE sal > 5000.

questions.q: The table ITEM has 6 rows. Kiran runs cur.execute('SELECT * FROM ITEM'), then r1 = cur.fetchone(), then r2 = cur.fetchmany(2).
p: (a) How many rows are in r2?
(b) What is the value of cur.rowcount now?
(c) How many rows will a following cur.fetchall() return?
questions.e: fetchone() takes 1 row and fetchmany(2) takes 2 more, so rowcount (rows retrieved so far) is 3 and 3 rows remain for fetchall().

questions.q: Which part of the CPU carries out arithmetic and logical operations?
questions.a: ALU|arithmetic logic unit|arithmetic and logic unit
questions.e: The Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) performs calculations and comparisons; the control unit directs the other parts.

questions.q: Which type of primary memory is volatile, i.e. it loses its contents when the power is switched off?
questions.e: RAM holds data and programs currently in use and is erased when the power goes off; ROM keeps its contents.

questions.q: System software that manages the hardware of a computer and provides an interface for the user, such as Windows or Linux, is called the ______.
questions.e: The operating system manages memory, processes and devices and lets the user interact with the computer.

questions.q: Convert the octal number 75 into decimal.
questions.e: 75 in octal = 7 x 8 + 5 = 61.

questions.q: Convert the decimal number 200 into hexadecimal.
questions.e: 200 = 12 x 16 + 8, and 12 is written as C in hexadecimal, so the answer is (C8)16.

questions.q: Which 8-bit encoding scheme was developed in India to represent the characters of Indian scripts?
questions.a: ISCII|Indian Script Code for Information Interchange
questions.e: ISCII (Indian Script Code for Information Interchange) was developed in the 1980s for Indian languages; Unicode later included these scripts.

questions.q: A language translator that converts a whole high-level language program into machine code in one go is called a ______.
questions.e: A compiler translates the entire program at once; an interpreter translates and runs one statement at a time.

questions.q: Convert the decimal fraction 0.625 into binary.
questions.e: Multiply the fraction by 2 repeatedly: 0.625 x 2 = 1.25 (1), 0.25 x 2 = 0.5 (0), 0.5 x 2 = 1.0 (1), giving (0.101)2.

questions.q: Which Unicode encoding uses a fixed length of 4 bytes for every character?
questions.e: UTF-32 always uses 32 bits (4 bytes) per character, whereas UTF-8 uses 1 to 4 bytes depending on the character.

questions.q: Convert the octal number 157 into binary.
questions.e: Replace each octal digit by 3 bits: 1 = 001, 5 = 101, 7 = 111, giving 001101111 = (1101111)2.

questions.q: Which logic gate gives the output 1 only when all its inputs are 1?
questions.e: An AND gate outputs 1 only if every input is 1; if any input is 0 the output is 0.

questions.q: In Boolean algebra, A . 0 = ______.
questions.e: AND with 0 always gives 0, whatever the value of A (Annulment law).

questions.q: How many rows are there in the truth table of a Boolean expression with 3 variables?
questions.e: With n variables there are 2^n input combinations, so 3 variables give 2^3 = 8 rows.

questions.q: Which logic gate gives the output 1 when its two inputs are different?
questions.e: XOR gives 1 for inputs 0, 1 and 1, 0, and gives 0 when both inputs are the same.

questions.q: Which logic gate is equivalent to an OR gate followed by a NOT gate?
questions.e: NOR = NOT(OR), i.e. (A + B)'; its output is the inverse of the OR output.

questions.q: By De Morgan's law, (A + B)' = ______.
questions.e: De Morgan's law: the complement of a sum is the product of the complements, so (A + B)' = A'.B'.

questions.q: What is the output of a NAND gate when both its inputs are 1?
questions.e: NAND is NOT(AND): 1 AND 1 = 1, and inverting it gives 0.

questions.q: In Boolean algebra, A + A' = ______.
questions.e: One of A and A' is always 1, so their OR is always 1 (Complement law).

questions.q: What is the value of the Boolean expression (A + B').C when A = 0, B = 1 and C = 1?
Simplify the Boolean expression A + A.B.
questions.e: By the Absorption law, A + A.B = A(1 + B) = A.1 = A.

questions.q: A two-input NOR gate gives the output 1 only when ______.
questions.e: NOR is NOT(OR); A + B is 0 only when both inputs are 0, so NOR is 1 only in that case.

questions.q: Which built-in function is used to accept a value typed by the user from the keyboard?
questions.e: input() reads a line typed by the user and always returns it as a string.

questions.q: Which symbol is used to begin a single-line comment in Python?
questions.e: Everything after # on a line is a comment and is ignored by the interpreter.

questions.q: What is the data type of the value of the expression 5 > 3 in Python?
questions.e: 5 > 3 is a comparison whose value is True, which is of type bool.

questions.q: What is the output of print(int(7.9) + int('3'))?
questions.e: int(7.9) truncates the decimal part to give 7, and int('3') converts the string to 3, so 7 + 3 = 10.

questions.q: Which of the following is a valid identifier in Python: 2total, total_2, total-2, for?
questions.e: An identifier cannot start with a digit, cannot contain - and cannot be a keyword such as for.

questions.q: What is the output of print('5' * 3)?
questions.e: * with a string and an integer repeats the string, so '5' * 3 is '555'.

questions.q: A program runs without any error message but gives a wrong result because a wrong formula was used. This is a ______ error.
questions.e: A logical error does not stop the program; it only makes the output wrong, so it is the hardest to find.

questions.q: What is the output of print(-19 // 4)?
questions.e: // is floor division: -19 / 4 = -4.75, and the floor (next lower integer) of -4.75 is -5.

questions.q: What is the output of print(3 + 4 * 2 ** 2 // 3)?
questions.e: ** first: 2 ** 2 = 4; then * and // from left to right: 4 * 4 = 16, 16 // 3 = 5; finally 3 + 5 = 8.

questions.q:
What is the output?
a, b = 3, 5
a, b = b, a + b
print(a, b)
questions.e: The right-hand side is evaluated first using the old values (5 and 3 + 5 = 8), then assigned, so a = 5 and b = 8.

p: (a) What is the output of print(x / y)?
(b) What is the output of print(x // y)?
(c) What is the output of print(x ** y)?
questions.e: / gives true division 3.5, // gives floor division 3, and ** is exponentiation: 7 ** 2 = 49.

questions.q: Which keyword skips the remaining statements of the current iteration and moves on to the next iteration of the loop?
questions.e: continue jumps to the next iteration; break leaves the loop altogether.

questions.q: Which statement does nothing and is used as a placeholder where a statement is required by the syntax?
questions.e: pass is a null statement, useful for an empty block such as if x > 0: pass.

questions.q: In Python, the block of statements that belongs to an if or a for statement is marked by ______.
questions.e: Python uses indentation (usually 4 spaces) to group statements into a block.
range(5, 0, -2) counts down by 2 from 5 and stops before 0, giving 5, 3 and 1.
The first true condition is x > 10, so only A is printed; the elif and else parts are then skipped.
With the default step of 1, range(10, 2) is empty because the start is already beyond the stop, so the body never runs.

questions.q:
What is the output?
i = 1
while i < 20:
    i = i * 3
print(i)
questions.e: i becomes 3, 9 and then 27; at 27 the condition i < 20 is False, so 27 is printed.

questions.q:
What is the output?
s = 0
for i in range(1, 5):
    s = s + i * i
print(s)

questions.e: The inner loop runs 1, 2 and 3 times for i = 0, 1 and 2, so 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 stars are printed.

questions.q:
What is the output?
n = 0
for i in range(1, 10):
    if i % 4 == 0:
        break
    n += i
print(n)
questions.e: 1, 2 and 3 are added; when i is 4 the loop ends before 4 is added, so n = 6.

questions.q:
What is the output?
x = 10
while x > 0:
    x -= 4
print(x)
questions.e: x becomes 6, 2 and then -2; at -2 the condition x > 0 is False, so -2 is printed.

questions.q: What is the output of print(len('CBSE'))?
questions.e: len() counts the characters: 'C', 'B', 'S', 'E' make 4.

questions.q: Which operator is used to join (concatenate) two strings?
questions.e: 'Hello' + 'World' gives 'HelloWorld'; * repeats a string instead.

questions.q: Which string method returns a copy of the string with all letters in lowercase?
questions.e: 'CBSE'.lower() gives 'cbse'; the original string is not changed.

questions.q: What is the output of print('Hello World'.lower().find('w'))?
questions.e: lower() gives 'hello world', in which 'w' is at index 6 (the space is at index 5).

questions.q: What is the output of print('ab' in 'cabin')?
questions.e: The in operator checks for a substring; 'ab' occurs in 'cabin' at index 1.

questions.q: What is the output of print('Computer'[-3:])?
questions.e: [-3:] takes the last three characters of the string.

questions.q: What is the output of print('-'.join('abc'))?
questions.e: join() places the separator '-' between the characters of 'abc'.

questions.q: What is the output of print('Hello'.partition('l'))?
questions.e: partition() splits at the first occurrence of the separator and returns a 3-element tuple: the part before, the separator and the part after.

questions.q: What is the output of print('Programming'[::3])?
questions.e: A step of 3 takes the characters at indices 0, 3, 6 and 9: 'P', 'g', 'm', 'n'.

questions.q:
What is the output?
s = 'Delhi'
r = ''
for ch in s:
    r = ch + r
print(r)
questions.e: Each character is added in front of r, so the string is built in reverse order.

questions.q: Which list method removes the first occurrence of a given value from a list?
questions.e: L.remove(x) deletes the first element equal to x; pop() removes by position instead.

questions.q: Lists in Python are ______, i.e. their elements can be changed in place.
questions.e: An assignment such as L[0] = 5 changes the list itself, so lists are mutable.

questions.q: What is the output of print(max([4, 9, 2, 7]))?
questions.e: max() returns the largest element of the list, which is 9.

questions.q:
What is the output?
L = [1, 2, 3]
L.extend([4, 5])
print(len(L))
questions.e: extend() adds each element of the given list, so L becomes [1, 2, 3, 4, 5].

questions.q: What is the output of print([1, 2, 3, 4, 5][1:4])?
questions.e: Slicing [1:4] takes the elements at indices 1, 2 and 3.

questions.q:
What is the output?
L = [4, 2, 6, 2]
print(L.count(2) + sum(L))
questions.e: 2 occurs twice and the sum of the elements is 14, so 2 + 14 = 16.

questions.q:
What is the output?
L = [3, 8, 5]
L.reverse()
print(L[0])
questions.e: reverse() changes the list in place to [5, 8, 3], so L[0] is 5.

questions.q:
What is the output?
L = [1, 2, 3]
L.append([4, 5])
print(len(L))
questions.e: append() adds its argument as one element, so the whole list [4, 5] becomes the fourth element.

questions.q:
What is the output?
L = [[1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]
print(L[1][2] + len(L))
questions.e: L[1] is [3, 4, 5], so L[1][2] is 5; L has 2 elements (two inner lists), so 5 + 2 = 7.

questions.q:
What is the output?
L = [5, 2, 9]
M = sorted(L)
print(L[0], M[0])
questions.e: sorted() returns a new sorted list [2, 5, 9] and leaves L unchanged, so L[0] is 5 and M[0] is 2.

questions.q: The elements of a tuple are written inside ______ brackets.
questions.e: A tuple is written as (1, 2, 3); square brackets are used for lists and curly brackets for dictionaries.

questions.q: Tuples are ______: once a tuple is created, its elements cannot be changed.
questions.e: Like strings, tuples are immutable sequences; lists are mutable.

questions.q: What is the output of print((4, 8, 2)[1])?
questions.e: Indexing starts at 0, so index 1 is the second element, 8.

questions.q: What is the output of print((1, 2) + (3,))?
questions.e: + joins (concatenates) two tuples into a new tuple.

questions.q:
What is the output?
T = (10, 20, 30, 20)
print(T.index(20))
questions.e: index() returns the position of the first occurrence, and the first 20 is at index 1.

questions.q: What is the output of print(sum((2, 4, 6)) // len((2, 4, 6)))?
questions.e: sum() gives 12 and len() gives 3, so 12 // 3 = 4.

questions.q: Which error is raised by the statement T[0] = 5 when T is a tuple?
questions.e: Tuples do not support item assignment, so Python raises TypeError: 'tuple' object does not support item assignment.

questions.q:
What is the output?
a, b, c = (7, 8, 9)
print(b)
questions.e: Tuple assignment unpacks the values in order, so a = 7, b = 8 and c = 9.

questions.q: What is the output of print(sorted((3, 1, 2)))?
questions.e: sorted() always returns a new list, even when it is given a tuple.

questions.q:
What is the output?
T = (1, (2, 3), 4)
print(len(T))
questions.e: The nested tuple (2, 3) counts as a single element, so T has 3 elements.

questions.q: What is the data type of the value (7) in Python?
questions.e: Brackets alone do not make a tuple; (7) is just the integer 7. A one-element tuple needs a comma: (7,).

questions.q:
What is the output?
T = (5, 10, 15, 20, 25)
print(T[1:4:2])
questions.e: The slice starts at index 1 and takes every second element before index 4, i.e. indices 1 and 3.

p: (a) What is the output of print(max(T))?
(b) What is the output of print(T[-1] - T[0])?
(c) What is the output of print(min(T) * 3)?
questions.e: The largest element is 9; T[-1] is 9 and T[0] is 4, so 9 - 4 = 5; the smallest element is 1, and 1 * 3 = 3.

questions.q: In a dictionary, every ______ must be unique.
questions.e: Keys must be unique (and immutable); values may be repeated.

questions.q: Which dictionary method returns all the key-value pairs as tuples?
questions.e: For {'a': 1}, items() gives dict_items([('a', 1)]).

questions.q: Which symbol separates a key from its value in a dictionary?
questions.e: Each pair is written as key: value, for example {'roll': 12}; commas separate the pairs.

questions.q:
What is the output?
D = {'x': 10, 'y': 20}
D['x'] = 30
print(D['x'] + D['y'])
questions.e: Assigning to an existing key replaces its value, so D['x'] becomes 30 and 30 + 20 = 50.
pop('b') removes the pair and returns its value 2; D is left with 2 pairs, so 2 + 2 = 4.

questions.q: What is the output of print(dict.fromkeys(['a', 'b'], 0))?
questions.e: fromkeys() creates a new dictionary with the given keys, each set to the given value 0.

questions.q:
What is the output?
D = {1: 'A', 2: 'B'}
D.update({2: 'C', 3: 'D'})
print(len(D))
questions.e: update() changes the value of the existing key 2 and adds the new key 3, so D has 3 pairs.

questions.q: Which exception is raised when D[k] is used and the key k is not present in the dictionary D?
questions.e: Accessing a missing key with square brackets raises KeyError; get() returns None instead.

questions.q: What is the output of print(list({'p': 1, 'q': 2}.values()))?
questions.e: values() gives the values in insertion order, and list() turns them into a list.
The counts are {'l': 2, 'e': 2, 'v': 1}, so D['l'] is 2 and D has 3 keys: 2 + 3 = 5.

questions.q:
What is the output?
D = {'a': 1, 'b': 2}
E = D.copy()
E['a'] = 100
print(D['a'])
questions.e: copy() makes a new dictionary, so changing E does not change D.
sorted() on a dictionary works on its keys and returns them as a sorted list.

questions.q: Which module provides the functions mean(), median() and mode()?
questions.e: These are in the statistics module: import statistics, then statistics.mean(L).

questions.q: Which keyword is used to load a module, such as math, into a program?
questions.e: import math makes the functions of the math module available as math.function_name().

questions.q:
What is the output?
import math
print(math.sqrt(49))
questions.e: math.sqrt() always returns a float, so the square root of 49 is printed as 7.0.

questions.q:
What is the output?
import math
print(math.ceil(4.2))
questions.e: ceil() gives the smallest integer not less than the number, so 4.2 becomes 5.

questions.q:
What is the output?
import math
print(math.pow(2, 3))
questions.e: math.pow() converts its arguments to float and returns a float, so 2 to the power 3 is 8.0.

questions.q:
What is the output?
import statistics
print(statistics.mode([2, 3, 3, 5, 2, 3]))
questions.e: mode() returns the most frequent value; 3 occurs three times and 2 only twice.

questions.q: Which function of the random module returns a random floating-point number from 0.0 up to, but not including, 1.0?
questions.e: random.random() returns a float x with 0.0 <= x < 1.0.

questions.q:
What is the output?
import math
print(math.fabs(-6))
questions.e: fabs() returns the absolute value as a float, so -6 becomes 6.0.

questions.q: How many different values can random.randrange(5, 20, 4) return?
questions.e: The possible values are 5, 9, 13 and 17; the next value, 21, is beyond the stop value 20.

questions.q:
What is the output?
import math
print(math.ceil(-2.7) + math.floor(2.7))

questions.q:
What is the output?
import statistics
print(statistics.median([4, 1, 8, 6]))

questions.q: Sending fake emails that appear to come from a trusted source, in order to steal passwords or bank details, is called ______.
questions.e: Phishing tricks users into revealing sensitive information through fraudulent emails, messages or websites.

questions.q: Presenting someone else's work or ideas as one's own without giving them credit is called ______.
questions.e: Plagiarism is a violation of intellectual property rights; it is avoided by citing the source.

questions.q: Discarded electronic devices, such as old mobile phones and computers, are called ______.
questions.e: E-waste contains toxic substances such as lead and mercury, so it must be reused, recycled or disposed of safely.

questions.q: Malware that locks or encrypts a user's files and demands money to restore access is called ______.
questions.e: Ransomware holds data to ransom, usually demanding payment in cryptocurrency.

questions.q: A malicious program that looks like useful, legitimate software but harms the computer once it is installed is called a ______.
questions.e: Like the Trojan horse of the Greek story, it hides its harmful purpose behind something that appears harmless.

questions.q: Deliberately posting insulting or provocative comments online to upset people and draw attention is called cyber ______.
questions.e: Cyber trolls post sarcastic, demeaning or provocative comments; the best response is usually to ignore and report them.

questions.q: A registered name, word, logo or symbol that identifies a company's products is protected by a ______.
questions.e: A trademark distinguishes the brand of one company from others; patents protect inventions.

questions.q: Which public licence lets creators share works such as images, music, films and writing under conditions like giving credit to the creator?
questions.e: Creative Commons (CC) licences are used for creative works; GPL is mainly used for software.

questions.q: Secretly listening to or intercepting private communication between two parties on a network is called ______.
questions.e: Eavesdropping is a cyber crime in which an attacker intercepts data such as calls, messages or emails without permission.

questions.q: Data such as browsing history and location collected about a user without his or her knowledge forms a ______ digital footprint.
questions.e: An active footprint is data the user shares intentionally, such as posts; a passive footprint is collected unintentionally.

questions.q: Which open source licence, used for software such as Linux, requires that modified versions of the software are also released under the same licence?
questions.a: GPL|General Public License|GNU GPL|GNU General Public License|General Public Licence
questions.e: The GNU GPL is a copyleft licence; the Apache licence lets modified versions be distributed under different terms.

questions.q: Which HTML tag is used to write internal CSS inside the head section of a page?
questions.e: Rules written inside <style></style> in the head apply only to that one page.

questions.q: Which HTML attribute is used to apply inline CSS to a single element?
questions.e: For example <p style="color: blue;"> styles only that paragraph.

questions.q: Which CSS property changes the size of the text?
questions.e: Sizes can be given in units such as px or em, e.g. font-size: 20px;

questions.q: Which CSS property is used to centre the text inside a paragraph?
questions.e: text-align: center; centres the text; other values include left, right and justify.

questions.q: Which CSS property sets the space between the content of an element and its border?
questions.e: Padding is inside the border, whereas margin is the space outside the border.

questions.q: The same paragraph is given a text colour by inline, internal and external CSS, each with a different value. Which type of CSS decides the colour that is finally shown?
questions.e: Inline CSS is the most specific because it is written on the element itself, so it overrides internal and external rules.

questions.q: What are unwanted bulk emails, usually advertisements, sent to many people called?
questions.e: Spam fills inboxes and may carry harmful links, so it should be deleted unopened.

questions.q: What is the record of everything a person does online, such as posts, searches and websites visited, called?
questions.e: A digital footprint can be very hard to delete, so we should think before posting anything online.

questions.q: What is repeatedly sending threatening, hurtful or humiliating messages to someone through social media or messaging apps called?
questions.e: Cyberbullying should be reported to a trusted adult or the platform, and the messages kept as evidence.

questions.q: Which security system monitors incoming and outgoing network traffic and blocks unauthorised access according to a set of rules?
questions.e: A firewall can be hardware, software or both; an antivirus, by contrast, scans files for malware.

questions.q: Which type of malware pretends to be a useful program, such as a free game, but secretly harms the computer once installed?
questions.e: Unlike a worm, a Trojan does not copy itself; it relies on the user being tricked into installing it.

questions.q: Riya gets an email saying her bank account will be blocked unless she clicks a link and enters her PIN. The link opens a page that looks exactly like her bank's website. What is this cyber crime called?
questions.e: Phishing uses fake messages and look-alike websites to steal details; banks never ask for a PIN by email.

questions.q: Which HTML tag holds information about the page, such as its title and links to style sheets, that is not shown in the page itself?
questions.e: <head> comes before <body>; <header> is different, as it is a visible section at the top of the page body.

questions.q: Which HTML tag inserts a line break without starting a new paragraph?
questions.e: <br> is an empty tag, so it has no closing tag.

questions.q: The text written inside which tag appears on the browser tab of a web page?
questions.e: The <title> tag is placed inside <head>, and its text is also used when the page is bookmarked.

questions.q: Which HTML tag draws a horizontal line across the page?
questions.e: hr stands for horizontal rule and is often used to separate sections of a page.

questions.q: Which heading tag displays the smallest heading?
questions.e: HTML has six heading levels, from <h1> (largest) to <h6> (smallest); there is no <h7>.

questions.q: Tags such as <br> and <hr> that have no closing tag and no content are called ______ elements.
questions.a: empty|void|empty elements|void elements|empty element|void element|empty tags|empty tag|singleton
questions.e: Container elements such as <p> have an opening tag, content and a closing tag; empty elements have only one tag.

questions.q: Which declaration, written as the very first line of a page, tells the browser that the document uses HTML5?
questions.e: The DOCTYPE is not an HTML tag; it is an instruction to the browser about which version of HTML to expect.

questions.q:
How many lines of text does the browser display for this code (assuming the window is wide enough)?
<p>One Two<br>Three</p><p>Four</p>
questions.e: The lines are "One Two", "Three" and "Four": <br> breaks the line inside the first paragraph and each <p> starts on a new line.

questions.q: Which input type creates a small box that can be ticked, letting the user choose more than one option from a group?
questions.e: Unlike radio buttons, any number of checkboxes in a group can be ticked at the same time.

questions.q: Which HTML tag creates a multi-line text box, for example for writing an address?
questions.e: Its rows and cols attributes set how many lines and characters are visible.

questions.q: Which HTML tag creates a drop-down list in a form?
questions.e: Each choice in the drop-down list is written with an <option> tag inside <select>.

questions.q: Which attribute of <input> stops a form from being submitted while that field is left empty?
questions.e: required is a Boolean attribute, so simply writing it is enough, e.g. <input type="text" required>.

questions.q: Which value of the method attribute of <form> sends the form data as part of the URL, so it is visible in the address bar?
questions.e: GET is unsuitable for passwords; POST sends the data in the body of the request instead of the URL.

questions.q:
A form contains:
<select name="city">
<option value="DL">Delhi</option>
<option value="MB">Mumbai</option>
</select>
If the user chooses Delhi, what value is sent for city when the form is submitted?
questions.e: The value attribute is what is sent to the server; the text between the option tags is only what the user sees.

questions.q: Which HTML tag is used to create a hyperlink?
questions.e: The <a> (anchor) tag makes text or an image clickable; <link> is used in the head, for example to attach a style sheet.

questions.q: Which attribute of <img> gives the file name or path of the image to display?
questions.e: src is short for source and is required; without it there is no image to show.

questions.q: Which image format supports simple animation and is widely used for small moving images on web pages?
questions.e: GIF supports animation but only 256 colours, so JPEG is preferred for photographs.

questions.q: Which value of the target attribute of <a> makes the linked page open in a new tab or window?
questions.e: _self, which opens the page in the same tab, is the default when target is not given.

questions.q: Is the link <a href="images/photo.jpg"> an absolute URL or a relative URL?
questions.e: A relative URL is found starting from the current page's folder; an absolute URL gives the full address beginning with http:// or https://.

questions.q: Which word, followed by a colon and an email address, is written in href to make a link that opens the user's email program?
questions.e: For example <a href="mailto:info@example.com"> opens a new email addressed to info@example.com.

questions.q:
Study this code:
<a href="page2.html"><img src="next.png" alt="Next"></a>
If the file next.png is missing, what text does the browser show in place of the image?
questions.e: The alt text is shown instead of the missing image, and it still works as a link to page2.html.

questions.q: Which HTML tag defines each item in an ordered or unordered list?
questions.e: li stands for list item and is used inside both <ol> and <ul>.

questions.q: Which HTML tag creates an ordered (numbered) list?
questions.e: Items in an <ol> are numbered 1, 2, 3 by default; the type attribute can change this to letters or Roman numerals.

questions.q: In a description list (<dl>), which tag holds the term that is being described?
questions.e: dt is the description term and dd is its description, which is shown indented below it.

questions.q: A list placed inside an item of another list is called a ______ list.
questions.e: Nested lists show sub-points, such as a bulleted list of fruits inside a numbered list of food groups.

questions.q: Which CSS property changes the bullets of an unordered list to squares?
questions.e: list-style-type: square; gives square bullets; other values include disc, circle and none.

questions.q:
Study this code:
<ol>
<li>Fruits
<ul><li>Apple</li><li>Mango</li></ul>
</li>
<li>Vegetables</li>
</ol>
What number is shown before Vegetables?
questions.e: Apple and Mango belong to the inner bulleted list, so they do not count in the outer numbered list.

questions.q: Which HTML tag defines an ordinary data cell in a table?
questions.e: td stands for table data; its text is left-aligned and not bold by default.

questions.q: Which tag gives a table a title that is shown above it by default?
questions.e: <caption> must be written immediately after the opening <table> tag.

questions.q: Which attribute of <table> sets the space between the border of a cell and its content?
questions.e: cellpadding is space inside each cell, whereas cellspacing is the space between neighbouring cells.

questions.q: A table row contains <td colspan="2"> followed by two ordinary <td> cells. How many columns does this row cover?
questions.e: The first cell covers 2 columns and the other two cover 1 each: 2 + 1 + 1 = 4.

questions.q: A table has 3 columns. Its first row is <tr><td rowspan="2">A</td><td>B</td><td>C</td></tr>. How many <td> tags must the second row have to fill it exactly?
questions.e: Cell A already occupies the first column of the second row, so only 2 more cells are needed.

questions.q: In the URL https://www.example.com/news.html, which part is the protocol?
questions.e: A URL is made of the protocol (https), the domain name (www.example.com) and the path to the file (news.html).

questions.q: Which technology lets people make voice calls over the internet instead of an ordinary telephone line?
questions.a: VoIP|voice over internet protocol|voice over IP
questions.e: VoIP turns the voice into data packets, which is how apps such as WhatsApp make calls.

questions.q: Which protocol is the secure version of HTTP that encrypts the data passing between the browser and the website?
questions.e: Browsers usually show a padlock for HTTPS sites; it should always be used for logins and payments.

questions.q: When you type www.example.com in a browser, which system is asked first to find the IP address of the server that holds the site?
questions.a: DNS|domain name system|domain name server|domain name service
questions.e: Computers find each other by IP address, so DNS lets people use easy-to-remember names instead of numbers.

questions.q: Which email protocol keeps messages on the mail server, so the same mailbox can be read from several devices?
questions.e: Because IMAP keeps mail on the server, a message read on a phone also shows as read on a laptop.

questions.q: Which protocol lets a user log in to a remote computer and work on it as if sitting at it, but sends everything, including passwords, without encryption?
questions.e: Because Telnet is unencrypted, SSH (Secure Shell) is now used for remote login instead.

questions.q: Which type of network covers a small area such as a school building or a computer lab?
questions.e: A LAN is usually owned by one organisation and offers high data transfer speeds.

questions.q: In which topology is every device connected to a central hub or switch?
questions.e: If one cable fails only that device is affected, but if the central device fails the whole network stops.

questions.q: What is the largest WAN in the world, connecting millions of networks across the globe?
questions.e: An intranet, by contrast, is a private network used only within one organisation.

questions.q: Which device regenerates a weak signal so that it can travel a longer distance in a network?
questions.e: Signals become weaker over long cables, so a repeater amplifies and resends them.

questions.q: Which transmission medium carries data as pulses of light through thin strands of glass?
questions.a: optical fibre|optical fiber|optical fibre cable|optical fiber cable|fibre optic cable|fiber optic cable|fibre optic|fiber optic|fibre|fiber
questions.e: Optical fibre gives very high speeds and is not affected by electrical interference.

questions.q: Which device connects different networks, such as a home LAN and the internet, and chooses the best path for data packets using IP addresses?
questions.e: A switch works within a single network, while a router forwards data between networks.

questions.q: Which device in a LAN sends data only to the computer it is meant for, instead of to all connected computers as a hub does?
questions.e: A switch learns the MAC address of each connected device, which reduces unnecessary traffic.

questions.q: How many cables are needed to connect 5 computers in a full mesh topology?
questions.e: Each pair needs one cable: n(n-1)/2 = 5 x 4 / 2 = 10.

questions.q: Which keyword sends a value back from a function to the statement that called it?
questions.e: Statements after return in the same function do not run, because return ends the function.

questions.q: The values passed to a function when it is called, such as 3 and 4 in add(3, 4), are called ______.
questions.e: The names in the def line that receive these values are called parameters (formal parameters).

questions.q: What value does a Python function return if it has no return statement?
questions.e: None is a special value meaning nothing; print(f()) for such a function prints None.

questions.q:

change()
print(x)

questions.q: What is the output of print([1, 2] + [3])?
questions.e: The + operator joins (concatenates) two lists; it does not add the numbers together.

questions.q: Which list method removes and returns the last element when no index is given?
questions.e: L.pop(0) would remove the first element instead, while remove() deletes by value, not position.

questions.q:

print(len(L))

questions.q: What is the output of print('ab' * 3)?
questions.e: Multiplying a string by a whole number repeats it that many times.

questions.q: Which string method converts all the letters of a string to capital letters?
questions.e: upper() returns a new string, e.g. "cbse".upper() gives "CBSE"; capitalize() changes only the first letter.
