s = "INDIA"
r = ""
for ch in s:
    r = ch + r
print(r)
questions.e: Each character is added to the front of r, so the string is built in reverse order.

questions.q: A computer program that holds a conversation with people through text or voice, such as a help assistant on a shopping website, is called a ______.
questions.e: A chatbot uses AI to understand messages and reply to them like a person would.

questions.q: The examples given to a machine learning model so that it can learn patterns, before it is tested, are called ______ data.
questions.e: A model first learns from training data and is then checked on separate testing data.

questions.q: A face-recognition system works well for some skin tones but makes many mistakes for others, because most of its training photos showed only some skin tones. What is this problem in AI called?
questions.e: When training data is unbalanced, the AI learns unfair patterns; this is called bias.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT an example of artificial intelligence?
questions.a: a calculator adding two numbers|calculator|a calculator
o: a phone that unlocks by recognising your face
a music app that suggests songs you may like
questions.e: A calculator only follows fixed rules; it does not learn from data or make decisions like an AI system.

questions.q: Meera asks a generative AI chatbot for a fact for her history project. It gives a confident, detailed answer that turns out to be completely made up. What is such false AI output commonly called?
questions.e: Generative AI can 'hallucinate', producing believable but false information, so facts should always be checked in reliable sources.

questions.q: What is the worldwide network of networks that links millions of computers called?
questions.e: The internet joins networks all over the world; it is the largest WAN.

questions.q: In which type of network do all computers have equal status and share files directly with each other, without a dedicated server?
questions.e: In a peer-to-peer network each computer can act as both client and server.

questions.q: Which wireless technology, common in homes, schools and cafes, connects devices to a network using radio signals?
questions.e: Wi-Fi sends data by radio signals, so no network cable is needed.

questions.q: Riya's school has a private website for notices and homework that only its students and teachers can open after logging in to the school network. This private network is an example of an ______.
questions.e: An intranet uses internet technology but is open only to the members of one organisation.

questions.q: A 600 MB file is downloaded at a steady speed of 5 MB per second. How many seconds does the download take?
questions.e: Time = size / speed = 600 / 5 = 120 seconds (2 minutes).

questions.q: What is the software that scans a computer to find and remove viruses called?
questions.e: Antivirus software detects and removes malicious programs; it should be kept updated.

questions.q: Unwanted emails sent in bulk, often advertisements or tricks, are called ______.
questions.e: Spam is unwanted bulk email; it is safest not to open its links or attachments.

questions.q: Which of these passwords is the strongest?
questions.e: A strong password is long and mixes capital and small letters, numbers and symbols, and is not easy to guess.

questions.q: A program that looks useful, such as a free game, but secretly harms the computer once installed is named after the wooden horse of a Greek legend. What is it called?
questions.e: Like the wooden horse that hid soldiers, a Trojan hides harmful code inside a program that seems harmless.

questions.q: A safe website's address begins with https:// and shows a padlock in the browser. What does the letter 's' in https stand for?
questions.e: HTTPS is HyperText Transfer Protocol Secure; it encrypts the data sent between your browser and the website.

questions.q: Kabir uses the same password for his email, his games account and his school portal. The games website is hacked and his password is leaked. Which of his accounts are now at risk?
questions.e: Anyone with the leaked password can try it on his other accounts, so each account should have its own password.

questions.q: Which HTML tag makes text bold?
questions.e: <b> (or <strong>) shows text in bold.

questions.q:
Fill in the blank so that the text 'Visit NCERT' becomes a link to https://ncert.nic.in
<a ______="https://ncert.nic.in">Visit NCERT</a>
questions.e: The href attribute of the <a> (anchor) tag gives the address the link opens.

questions.q:
Study this HTML:
<ol type="A">
<li>Rice</li>
<li>Wheat</li>
<li>Maize</li>
</ol>
How is the second item shown in the browser?
questions.e: <ol> makes an ordered list and type="A" numbers it with capital letters, so the items are A, B and C.

questions.q: In which topology are all devices connected to one main cable called the backbone?
questions.e: In a bus topology every device is joined to a single backbone cable.

questions.q: In which topology are all the computers connected one after another in a closed loop, so that data passes from one computer to the next?
questions.e: In a ring, each computer is joined to the two next to it; a break in the ring can stop the whole network.

questions.q: Which network device regenerates a weak signal so that it can travel a longer distance?
questions.e: Signals weaken over long cables; a repeater boosts them and sends them on.

questions.q: Which device in a LAN sends the data it receives to every computer connected to it, instead of only to the computer it is meant for?
questions.e: A hub broadcasts data to all its ports, whereas a switch sends it only to the intended computer.

questions.q: 5 computers are to be joined in a mesh topology, with a separate cable between every pair of computers. How many cables are needed?

What is the output?
first = "Sun"
second = "day"
print(second + first)
questions.e: The + operator joins (concatenates) strings in the order written, so second comes first, with no space added.

questions.q: Which Python function converts a string such as "25" into a whole number?
questions.e: int("25") gives the integer 25, which can then be used in calculations.

questions.q:
The user types 4 and then 6 when this program runs. What is the output?
a = int(input())
b = int(input())
print(a * b + a % b)
questions.e: a * b = 24 and 4 % 6 = 4 (6 does not go into 4), so 24 + 4 = 28.

questions.q: Which spreadsheet function finds the largest value in a range?
questions.e: =MAX(range) gives the largest number; =MIN(range) gives the smallest.

questions.q: Write the formula that finds the smallest value in cells B2 to B10.
questions.e: MIN returns the smallest number, and B2:B10 is the range from B2 to B10.

questions.q: Cells C1 to C6 contain 45, 78, 32, 90, 66 and 28. What does =COUNTIF(C1:C6,">=40") return?
questions.e: COUNTIF counts the cells that meet the condition: 45, 78, 90 and 66 are at least 40, so 4.

questions.q: What is a diagram that shows the steps of an algorithm using special shapes joined by arrows called?
questions.e: A flowchart is a picture of an algorithm; arrows show the order in which the steps are carried out.

questions.q: Which flowchart shape is used for a process step, such as 'Total = A + B'?
questions.e: A rectangle shows a process or calculation step in a flowchart.

questions.q: Algorithm: Step 1 Start. Step 2 Let N = 9. Step 3 If N divided by 2 leaves a remainder of 0, print 'Even', else print 'Odd'. Step 4 Stop. What is printed?
questions.e: 9 divided by 2 gives 4 remainder 1, so the condition is false and 'Odd' is printed.

questions.q: Which type of computer language uses short codes called mnemonics, such as ADD and MOV, instead of 0s and 1s?
questions.e: Assembly language uses mnemonics, which are easier to remember than binary codes.

questions.q: What is the general name for a program, such as a compiler, interpreter or assembler, that converts a program into machine language?
questions.e: Compilers, interpreters and assemblers are all language translators.

questions.q: What is the process of finding and removing errors from a computer program called?
questions.e: Errors in a program are called bugs, so removing them is called debugging.

questions.q: A program written in the machine language of one type of computer may not run on a different type of computer. So, is machine language machine-dependent or machine-independent?
questions.e: Machine language is written for one particular type of processor, so it is machine-dependent.

questions.q: Riya wants a translator that runs her program one line at a time and stops as soon as it reaches a line with an error. Which translator should she use?
questions.e: An interpreter translates and runs one line at a time, so it stops at the first error it finds.

questions.q: A program should multiply two numbers but adds them instead. It runs without any error message but gives wrong answers. What type of error is this?
questions.e: A logical error lets the program run but gives wrong results, because the steps themselves are wrong.

questions.q: What is a harmful program that attaches itself to files and spreads from one computer to another, damaging data, called?
questions.e: A computer virus spreads through infected files, downloads and pen drives, and can damage or delete data.

questions.q: A password that is long and mixes capital letters, small letters, numbers and symbols, such as Tr33-Hous3!Kite, is called a strong password or a weak password?
questions.e: Long passwords that mix different kinds of characters are much harder to guess, so they are strong.

questions.q: What is the software that finds and removes viruses from a computer called?
questions.e: Antivirus software scans files and removes harmful programs; it should be kept up to date.

questions.q: Rohan makes copies of a paid computer game and sells them to his friends without the maker's permission. What is this illegal act called?
questions.e: Copying or selling software without permission breaks copyright law and is called software piracy.

questions.q: Sana uses a photo from a website in her project and writes the website's name and the photographer's name below it. What is this practice of giving credit to the source called?
questions.e: Citing the source gives credit to the creator, which avoids plagiarism.

questions.q: Someone guessed Amit's password and logged in to his account. Which extra security step, which asks for a one-time code sent to his phone as well as his password, would best stop this happening again?
questions.a: two-factor authentication|two factor authentication|2FA|two-step verification|two step verification|multi-factor authentication|multi factor authentication
questions.e: With two-factor authentication, a stolen password alone is not enough, because the attacker also needs the code sent to Amit's phone.

questions.q: What does WWW stand for?
questions.e: The World Wide Web is the collection of web pages that we open on the internet.

questions.q: In the email address meera.k@example.com, what is the part before the @ sign called?
questions.e: An email address is made of a username, the @ sign and a domain name.

questions.q: Kavya types 'science project ideas' into a website, which then shows her a list of links to useful pages. What kind of website is she using?
questions.e: A search engine finds web pages that match the words (keywords) typed in.

questions.q: Mohan sends an email to five classmates, with all five addresses in the To field. One classmate clicks Reply All. How many people receive this reply?
questions.e: Reply All goes to the sender (Mohan) and the other 4 receivers: 1 + 4 = 5.

questions.q: Name one software used to make slide presentations.
questions.e: PowerPoint, LibreOffice Impress, Google Slides and Keynote are all presentation software.

questions.q: What is a ready-made design, with matching colours, fonts and backgrounds, that can be applied to all slides at once called?
questions.e: A theme gives all slides a matching look in one step.

questions.q: What is the arrangement of boxes, such as a title box and a content box, on a slide called?
questions.e: A slide layout decides where the placeholders for titles, text and pictures go.

questions.q: Rina wants to write reminders for herself under each slide that the audience will not see during the slide show. Where should she type them?
questions.e: Speaker notes are for the presenter only and are not shown on the screen during the slide show.

questions.q: A presentation has 20 slides. Each slide is set to change automatically after 30 seconds. How many minutes will the whole slide show take?
questions.e: 20 x 30 = 600 seconds, and 600 / 60 = 10 minutes.

questions.q: In Scratch, what is each different picture of a sprite, which can be switched to make it look as if it is walking, called?
questions.e: Switching quickly between costumes makes a sprite look as if it is moving.

questions.q: In Scratch, which block category has the block that makes a sprite show a speech bubble saying Hello! for 2 seconds?
questions.e: Looks blocks change how a sprite appears, including speech and thought bubbles.

questions.q: Which Scratch block category has blocks such as 'move 10 steps' and 'turn 15 degrees'?
questions.e: Motion blocks move and turn sprites.

questions.q: A sprite starts at x: 0. Its script has a 'repeat 5' block containing 'change x by 20', followed by a 'change x by -30' block. What is the final value of x?
In Scratch, the variable score is set to 0. Then a 'repeat 6' block runs; inside it is an 'if score < 3 then' block containing 'change score by 1'. What is the final value of score?
questions.e: The score goes up by 1 only while it is less than 3: 1, 2, 3; in the last three repeats the condition is false, so it stays 3.

questions.q: In a shop bill, A1 holds the number of pens (3) and B1 holds the price of one pen (15). C1 holds a delivery charge of 10. What value does =A1*B1+C1 give?
questions.e: Multiplication is done first: 3 x 15 = 45, then 45 + 10 = 55.

questions.q: Who is known as the father of the computer?
questions.e: Charles Babbage designed the Analytical Engine in the 1830s, which had the main parts of a modern computer.

questions.q: What is the main circuit board inside a computer, to which the CPU, memory and other parts are connected, called?
questions.e: The motherboard is the main circuit board that connects all the parts of a computer so they can work together.

questions.q: Sara uses the same computer to write a letter, draw a picture, play a game and do her sums. Which characteristic of a computer does this show?
questions.e: Versatility means a computer can do many different kinds of work.

questions.q: Rahul saved his class photos on a computer five years ago and can still open them today. Which characteristic of a computer does this show?
questions.e: A computer can store a large amount of data for a long time and give it back whenever needed.

questions.q: Ravi typed 50 instead of 15 while entering marks, so the computer showed a wrong total. Which term means that wrong input gives wrong output?
questions.e: GIGO stands for Garbage In, Garbage Out: a computer is only as accurate as the data and instructions it is given.

questions.q: Details such as your full name, home address and phone number are called ______ information, and should be kept private online.
questions.e: Personal information can be used by strangers to find or trick you, so share it only with trusted people.

questions.q: Should you share your password with your friends? (yes/no)
questions.e: A password should be kept secret; only your parents or guardians may need to know it.

questions.q: What is it called when someone breaks into another person's computer or account without permission?
questions.e: Hacking means getting into a computer or account without permission, and it is a cyber crime.

questions.q: You finish using a computer in the school lab where you were logged in to your account. What should you do before leaving?
questions.e: Logging out stops the next person from using your account on a shared computer.

questions.q: Kabir wants to post on a public website. Which of these is safe for him to share?
o: His school timetable with his photo
questions.e: Personal details such as your address, phone number, photo and where you will be can help strangers find you, so keep them private.

questions.q: Ananya's tablet asks her to install updates for its operating system and antivirus. Why is it a good idea to install them?
questions.a: Updates fix security weaknesses and protect against new viruses
o: Updates always make the screen bigger
Updates delete old files to free space
Updates switch off the internet to keep it safe
questions.e: Updates repair weak points that attackers could use and teach the antivirus about new threats, so devices stay safer.

questions.q: Which one of these is hardware: keyboard, MS Paint, Scratch or Windows?
questions.e: A keyboard is a physical part you can touch; the others are software.

questions.q: Which hardware part inside the computer case changes the mains electricity into the power that the other parts need?
questions.a: SMPS|power supply|power supply unit|PSU|switch mode power supply
questions.e: The SMPS (Switch Mode Power Supply) gives the right power to the motherboard, drives and other parts.

questions.q: Tanya installs a new game on her laptop. Is the game hardware or software?
questions.e: A game is a set of instructions that cannot be touched, so it is software (application software).

questions.q: Ishaan's new printer is connected but does not print, because a small program that lets the computer talk to the printer is missing. What is this program called?
questions.e: A device driver is software that helps the operating system control a hardware device.

questions.q: Look at this list: Windows, MS Paint, Linux, Scratch. How many of these are system software?
questions.e: Windows and Linux are operating systems (system software); MS Paint and Scratch are application software.

questions.q: Which input device is used to point at and click on things on the screen?
questions.e: A mouse moves the pointer on the screen and lets you click, double-click and drag.

questions.q: Which input device with a stick and buttons is mostly used to play games?
questions.e: A joystick is moved in different directions to control objects in games.

questions.q: A teacher wants to show a video to the whole class on a large white screen. Which output device should she use?
questions.e: A projector shows the computer's output in a large size on a screen or wall.

questions.q: In an exam, students fill in circles on an answer sheet with a pencil or pen, and a machine checks the sheets. Which input device reads these marks?
questions.e: An OMR (Optical Mark Reader) senses the filled-in marks on a sheet; MICR reads the special ink numbers on cheques.

questions.q: What is a collection of related web pages under one address, such as cbse.gov.in, called?
questions.e: A website is a group of linked web pages that share one address.

questions.q: What is the main or first page of a website called?
questions.e: The home page is the starting page of a website, with links to its other pages.

questions.q: What is a word or picture on a web page that takes you to another page when you click it called?
questions.e: A hyperlink joins one web page to another; the pointer usually changes to a hand over it.

questions.q: Kiran wants to send a letter with a photo to her cousin in another city, and have it reach in seconds over the internet. Which internet service should she use?
questions.e: Email lets you send messages and attachments such as photos over the internet.

questions.q: Riya visits a useful website often and wants to open it later without typing its address again. What should she save in her web browser?
questions.e: A bookmark (also called a favourite) saves a web page's address in the browser so it can be opened with one click.

questions.q: In the web address https://www.cbse.gov.in, what does the part 'gov' tell you about the kind of website?
questions.a: government|government website|it is a government website|a government website
questions.e: 'gov' shows that the website belongs to the government; 'in' shows that it belongs to India.

questions.q: What is the full form of ROM?
questions.e: ROM stands for Read Only Memory; it keeps the start-up instructions even when the power is off.

questions.q: Is RAM primary memory or secondary memory?
questions.e: RAM is primary (main) memory that the CPU uses directly while working.

questions.q: What is saving files on servers over the internet, so that you can open them from any device, called?
questions.e: Cloud storage keeps your files online on servers, so you only need an internet connection to reach them.

questions.q: Rohan wants to give a 2 GB video to a friend using a small device he can carry in his pocket. Which of these should he use: pen drive, RAM, ROM or cache memory?
questions.a: pen drive|pendrive|USB drive|flash drive|USB flash drive
questions.e: A pen drive is portable secondary storage; RAM, ROM and cache are fixed inside the computer.

questions.q: Aisha was typing a story when the power went off before she saved it. Why was her story lost?
questions.a: It was only in RAM, which loses data without power
questions.e: Unsaved work is kept in RAM, which is volatile; saving copies it to secondary storage such as the hard disk.

questions.q: Arrange these from fastest to slowest: RAM, hard disk, cache memory.
questions.e: Cache is closest to the CPU and fastest, RAM comes next, and the hard disk is the slowest of the three.

questions.q: Which is larger: 1 MB or 1 KB?
questions.e: 1 MB = 1024 KB, so 1 MB is larger.

questions.q: Complete the order of memory units: KB, MB, GB, ______
questions.e: After gigabyte (GB) comes terabyte (TB); 1 TB = 1024 GB.

questions.q: Each photo is 256 KB. How many such photos make 2 MB? (1 MB = 1024 KB)
Name one operating system.
questions.e: Windows, Linux, macOS, Android and iOS are all operating systems.

questions.q: Which bar at the very top of a window shows the name of the open program or file?
questions.e: The title bar shows the window's name and holds the Minimise, Maximise and Close buttons.

questions.q: What is the process of starting a computer, when the operating system is loaded into memory, called?
questions.e: When you switch on a computer, it boots: the operating system loads into RAM so the computer is ready to use.

questions.q: Shreya has Paint, a web browser and Scratch open at the same time and switches between them. Which feature of the operating system allows this?
questions.e: Multitasking means the operating system lets more than one program run at the same time.

questions.q: Sonu types commands to see his files, while Priya clicks icons and menus with a mouse. Which kind of interface is Priya using?
questions.e: A Graphical User Interface (GUI) uses pictures such as icons and menus; Sonu is using a Character User Interface (CUI).

questions.q: In Windows, what happens to a file that is deleted by pressing Shift+Delete?
questions.a: It is deleted permanently without going to the Recycle Bin
o: It goes to the Recycle Bin
It is copied to the desktop
questions.e: Shift+Delete skips the Recycle Bin, so the file cannot be restored from there.

questions.q: In Scratch, which block category contains 'play sound Meow until done'?
questions.e: Sound blocks play sounds and change the volume.

questions.q: In Scratch, which block category has blocks that do sums and compare numbers, such as '( ) + ( )' and '( ) > ( )'?
questions.e: Operators blocks do maths (+, -, *, /) and comparisons (>, <, =).

questions.q: In Scratch, what is a named store that holds a value which can change while the project runs, such as a game's score, called?
questions.e: A variable holds a value that blocks such as 'set score to 0' and 'change score by 1' can update.

questions.q: Tina wants her cat sprite to say 'Meow' only when someone clicks on the cat. Which Events block should start the script?
questions.a: when this sprite clicked|this sprite clicked|when sprite clicked
questions.e: The 'when this sprite clicked' block runs its script each time the sprite is clicked.

questions.q: With the pen down, a sprite runs 'repeat 3 [move 100 steps, turn right 120 degrees]'. What shape does it draw?
questions.e: It draws 3 equal sides and turns 3 x 120 = 360 degrees in all, so it makes an equilateral triangle.

questions.q: Which shortcut key makes the selected text italic?
questions.e: Ctrl+I makes text slanting (italic); press it again to remove italics.

questions.q: Which shortcut key underlines the selected text?
questions.e: Ctrl+U underlines, Ctrl+B makes text bold and Ctrl+I makes it italic.

questions.q: Which shortcut key cuts the selected text so that it can be moved to another place?
questions.e: Ctrl+X removes the text and keeps it ready to paste with Ctrl+V.

questions.q: Amit typed 'teh' and the word processor changed it to 'the' by itself as he typed. Which feature did this?
questions.e: AutoCorrect fixes common typing mistakes automatically as you type.

questions.q: A computer is a ______ thing, like a fan or a car.
questions.e: A computer does not eat, grow or breathe. It is a non-living machine.

questions.q: A computer does sums much ______ than we can.
questions.e: A computer can do thousands of sums in a second.

questions.q: If we give a computer the right instructions, it gives ______ answers every time.
questions.e: A computer does not make mistakes in its work when we give it the right instructions.

questions.q: Riya asked the computer to add 25 and 15. What answer did it show?
questions.e: 25 + 15 = 40. A computer does such sums quickly and correctly.

questions.q: A bulb, a fan and a computer all use electricity. Which one can do many different jobs, like drawing and playing songs?
questions.e: A bulb only gives light and a fan only moves air, but a computer can do many kinds of work.

questions.q: A small ______ on top of the monitor lets us see each other on a video call.
questions.e: A webcam takes pictures and videos of us for video calls.

questions.q: A laptop has a flat square below the keys that works like a mouse. It is called a ______.
questions.e: We move a finger on the touchpad to move the pointer on a laptop.

questions.q: A computer with a CPU box, a monitor, a keyboard and a mouse kept on a table is called a ______ computer.
questions.e: A desktop computer stays in one place on a desk or table.

questions.q: Keyboard is to type as mouse is to ______.
questions.e: We type with the keyboard and click or point with the mouse.

questions.q: The teacher wants the whole class to hear a song from the computer. Should she use headphones or speakers?
questions.e: Speakers play sound loudly for everyone. Headphones let only one person hear.

questions.q: Writers use computers to ______ stories.
questions.e: Writers type their stories on a computer and can change them easily.

questions.q: In a library, a computer keeps a list of all the ______.
questions.e: A library computer shows which books are there and who has taken them.

questions.q: Which place uses computers to keep a record of letters and parcels: a post office, a park or a pond?
questions.a: post office|a post office|the post office
questions.e: Post offices use computers to keep track of letters and parcels.

questions.q: Engineers use computers to plan and draw houses and ______.
questions.e: Engineers draw plans of houses, buildings and bridges on computers.

questions.q: At a shop, the computer reads the black and white lines on a packet to find its price. These lines are called a ______.
questions.e: The computer reads the barcode and shows the price on the bill.

questions.q: A smartphone can make calls and also take ______.
questions.e: A smartphone has a camera, so it can take photos and videos.

questions.q: Smart devices like phones and tablets can work without a wire because they have a ______.
questions.e: A battery stores electricity. We charge it and then use the device anywhere.

questions.q: Many smartphones open when we touch them with our ______.
questions.e: Many phones read our fingerprint to open safely.

questions.q: A robot ______ cleaner moves around the house and cleans the floor by itself.
questions.e: A robot vacuum cleaner is a smart device that cleans floors on its own.

questions.q: Meera says 'Play a song' and her smart speaker plays one. Which part of the speaker hears her voice?
questions.e: A smart speaker has a microphone that picks up our voice.

questions.q: We should not keep the computer in direct ______, as it can get too hot.
questions.e: Strong sunlight can heat up and harm the computer.

questions.q: We should never throw or ______ the mouse.
questions.e: Dropping or banging the mouse can break it.

questions.q: After using the computer for some time, we should rest our ______ by looking away from the screen.
questions.e: Looking away from the screen now and then keeps our eyes healthy.

questions.q: Riya's laptop has become very hot. She should switch it off and let it ______ down.
questions.e: A hot laptop should be switched off and allowed to cool.

questions.q: Arjun wants to clean his keyboard. Before he cleans it, he should ______ the computer.
questions.e: We always switch off the computer before cleaning it, to stay safe.

questions.q: When Caps Lock is on, a small ______ glows on the keyboard.
questions.e: The small light tells us that Caps Lock is on.

questions.q: How many Shift keys are there on a keyboard?
questions.e: There is one Shift key on the left and one on the right.

questions.q: Holding down Shift and pressing the 1 key types the ______ mark.
questions.e: The 1 key also has the ! sign on it. Shift gives us the top sign on a key.

questions.q: Pressing Enter two times leaves an empty ______ between two lines.
questions.e: Each press of Enter starts a new line, so two presses leave one empty line.

questions.q: Riya typed 'BAG' because Caps Lock was on. Which key should she press to type small letters again?
questions.e: Pressing Caps Lock again turns it off, so letters come out small.

questions.q: We hold the mouse with the ______ of our hand resting on it.
questions.e: The palm rests on the mouse and the fingers press the buttons.

questions.q: We move the mouse on a soft, flat mat called a ______.
questions.e: A mouse pad helps the mouse move smoothly.

questions.q: On a web page, when the pointer is on a link, it changes into a small ______.
questions.e: The hand shape tells us that we can click there.

questions.q: When the computer is busy, the pointer may turn into a spinning ______.
questions.e: The spinning circle tells us to wait while the computer works.

questions.q: Arjun clicks once on a file icon. Does the file open, or does it get selected?
questions.e: A single click selects an icon. A double click opens it.

questions.q: The big white area where we draw in Paint is called the ______.
questions.e: We draw our pictures on the canvas.

questions.q: In Paint, we choose a colour from the colour ______.
questions.e: The colour palette shows many colours to choose from.

questions.q: Meera made a wrong line in Paint. Which button takes back her last step?
questions.e: Undo removes the last thing we did.

questions.q: Meera wants to open her drawing again tomorrow. Before closing Paint, she must ______ it.
questions.e: Saving keeps the drawing in the computer so we can open it later.

questions.q: Which shape in Paint draws a box with round corners?
questions.e: The Rounded rectangle shape draws a box with curved corners.

questions.q: At the bottom-right of the taskbar, we can see the ______ and the date.
questions.e: The taskbar shows the time and date at the bottom-right.

questions.q: After clicking Start, we click the ______ icon to see the Shut down option.
questions.e: The Power icon shows Sleep, Shut down and Restart.

questions.q: We should not press the power button again and again while the computer is ______.
questions.e: The computer takes a little time to start. We should wait patiently.

questions.q: Some computers ask for a ______ before showing the desktop, to keep them safe.
questions.e: A password or PIN stops others from using our computer.

questions.q: To shut down, Meera does these steps: click Start, click Power, click Shut down. Which step comes second?
questions.e: First Start, then Power, then Shut down.

questions.q: After some time on the screen, we should take a ______ and play outside.
questions.e: Too much screen time is not good for our eyes and body.

questions.q: We should ask our parents before we ______ any new game or app.
questions.e: Some games and apps can be harmful, so we ask an adult first.

questions.q: We should be ______ to others online, just like in real life.
questions.e: Good manners matter online too.

questions.q: A friendly person in a game asks for your photo. What should you say: yes or no?
questions.e: We never send our photos to people we meet online.

questions.q: A message says: 'Type your mother's phone number to get free coins.' Should Arjun type the number? Answer yes or no.
questions.e: Such messages are tricks. Arjun should not share it and should tell his parents.

questions.q: We should switch off the computer before ______ it.
questions.e: Cleaning a computer while it is on can give a shock or harm its parts.

questions.q: We should not eat near the keyboard, because food ______ can fall between the keys.
questions.e: Crumbs stuck between the keys can stop them from working.

questions.q: We should not keep the computer in direct ______, because the heat can harm it.
questions.e: Too much heat from the sun can damage the parts of a computer.

questions.q: We can use a soft ______ to clean dust from between the keys.
questions.e: A soft brush removes dust gently without scratching the keys.

questions.q: Antivirus software must be kept ______ so that it can catch new viruses.
questions.e: New viruses come out often, so the antivirus needs new updates to find them.

questions.q: Arjun's little brother bangs the keys hard. Arjun tells him to press the keys ______.
questions.e: Banging the keys can break them, so keys should be pressed gently.

questions.q: Meera's friend gives her a pen drive with a game on it. Before opening it, she should ______ it with antivirus software.
questions.e: A pen drive from someone else may carry a virus, so it should be scanned first.

questions.q: A computer can do thousands of sums in just one ______.
questions.e: Computers are very fast and can do a huge number of sums every second.

questions.q: A computer cannot think or decide by itself, because it has no ______ of its own.
questions.e: A computer has no IQ; it only follows the instructions we give it.

questions.q: If we give wrong data, the computer gives a wrong result. This is called GIGO: Garbage In, Garbage ______.
questions.e: GIGO means that wrong input gives wrong output.

questions.q: Riya's computer works out 99 x 99 in less than a second, and the answer is right. This shows speed and ______.
questions.e: Working fast shows speed, and giving the right answer (9801) shows accuracy.

questions.q: Arjun wanted to add 25 and 50, but typed 25 + 5. The computer showed 30. Who made the mistake: the computer or Arjun?
questions.e: 25 + 5 = 30 is correct; the input was wrong, so the output was wrong (GIGO).

questions.q: A ______ is an output device that shows a big picture on a wall or a white screen in class.
questions.e: A projector takes the picture from the computer and shows it in a large size.

questions.q: Find the odd one out: mouse, keyboard, monitor, scanner.
questions.e: The monitor is an output device; the other three are input devices.

questions.q: Meera scans her drawing and then prints a copy of it. Which device does she use first: the scanner or the printer?
questions.e: The scanner (input) first puts the drawing into the computer; then the printer (output) gives it on paper.

questions.q: After using our email on a school computer, we must ______ so that others cannot open it.
questions.e: Logging out closes our account so that the next user cannot see it.

questions.q: A strong password mixes letters, numbers and ______.
questions.e: Symbols like @ and # make a password harder to guess.

questions.q: Our name, address and phone number are personal details. We should keep them ______ online.
questions.e: Strangers can misuse personal details, so we never share them online.

questions.q: If someone keeps sending hurtful messages, we should ______ that person and tell an adult.
questions.e: Blocking stops the messages, and an adult can help to report the bully.

questions.q: A safe website address starts with ______ and shows a small lock sign.
questions.e: The 's' in https means secure; the data sent to the website is locked.

questions.q: On a keyboard, Ctrl stands for ______.
questions.e: Ctrl is the Control key; it is used with other keys, like Ctrl + C.

questions.q: The ______ key turns the numeric keypad on and off.
questions.e: When Num Lock is on, the numeric keypad types numbers.

questions.q: Arjun has typed a long story. Which key takes him one screen down at a time?
questions.e: Page Down moves one screen down, and Page Up moves one screen up.

questions.q: Caps Lock is on. Riya holds Shift and presses the R key. Will she get a capital R or a small r?
questions.e: When Caps Lock is on, Shift works the other way and types small letters.

questions.q: We keep the mouse on a flat, soft sheet called a mouse ______.
questions.e: A mouse pad helps the mouse move smoothly.

questions.q: Clicking the left button three times quickly is called a ______ click.
questions.e: In a typing program, a triple click selects a whole paragraph.

questions.q: A ______ mouse has a small rubber ball under it.
questions.e: Old mice had a ball under them; when it rolled, the pointer moved.

questions.q: A laptop has a flat touch area that works in place of a mouse. It is called a ______.
questions.e: We move a finger on the touchpad to move the pointer.

questions.q: Arjun is left-handed. In the mouse settings, he can ______ the left and right buttons.
questions.e: Windows lets us switch the main (primary) and other (secondary) buttons for left-handed use.

questions.q: CU stands for ______ Unit.
questions.e: The Control Unit (CU) controls all the work inside the computer.

questions.q: The monitor is also called the VDU. VDU stands for Visual Display ______.
questions.e: VDU means Visual Display Unit, as it displays words and pictures.

questions.q: The monitor, keyboard and mouse are joined by cables to the ______.
questions.e: All the parts are connected to the CPU, which does the main work.

questions.q: A computer adds 245 and 378 to get 623. Which part of the CPU does this sum?
questions.a: ALU|Arithmetic Logic Unit|Arithmetic and Logic Unit
questions.e: The ALU does all sums and comparisons: 245 + 378 = 623.

questions.q: Data goes in through input devices, is worked on in the ______, and comes out through output devices.
questions.e: The CPU processes the data between input and output.

questions.q: Riya types 6 x 7. While the sum is being done, which unit of the CPU keeps the numbers 6 and 7?
questions.e: The Memory Unit stores data and results; the ALU works out 6 x 7 = 42.

questions.q: The clock and the date are shown at the right end of the ______.
questions.e: The taskbar runs along the bottom of the screen and shows the time and date at its right end.

questions.q: The ______ option lets the computer rest using little power, and it wakes up quickly.
questions.e: In Sleep, the computer saves power and starts again quickly when we press a key or move the mouse.

questions.q: Before we shut down the computer, we should save and ______ all open programs.
questions.e: Saving and closing programs keeps our work safe before the computer turns off.

questions.q: Riya wants back a drawing she deleted. She opens the Recycle Bin, right-clicks it and chooses ______.
questions.e: Restore puts the file back where it was before it was deleted.

questions.q: Arjun switches off the main switch without shutting down the computer. What can happen to his unsaved work?
questions.a: lost|it is lost|it may be lost|lose|it can be lost|gets lost
questions.e: Without a proper shut down, unsaved work is lost and the computer can be harmed.

questions.q: In Paint, the ______ shape draws a line that we can then bend.
questions.e: With the Curve shape we draw a line and then drag to bend it.

questions.q: In Paint, the ______ button turns the picture upside down or on its side.
questions.e: Rotate turns the picture, for example by 90 or 180 degrees.

questions.q: In Paint, which button cuts away everything outside the selected part of the picture?
questions.e: After selecting a part, Crop keeps only that part and removes the rest.

questions.q: Meera wants to make her Paint picture half its size, not just look smaller on screen. Which button should she use?
questions.e: Resize changes the real size of the picture; the Magnifier only zooms the view.

questions.q: In a library, computers keep a record of all the ______.
questions.e: Library computers show which books are there and who has borrowed them.

questions.q: In hospitals, computers help doctors to check how our ______ is beating.
questions.e: Machines with computers show the heartbeat on a screen.

questions.q: In car factories, ______ controlled by computers help to make cars.
questions.e: Computer-controlled robots do jobs like painting and fixing parts.

questions.q: Computers help to change the traffic ______ at busy crossings.
questions.e: Computers switch the traffic lights from red to green at set times.

questions.q: Meera's family wants to find the road to her nani's village. Which helps them: online maps or online shopping?
questions.e: Online maps on a computer or phone show roads and the way to a place.

questions.q: A ticket machine prints one ticket every 2 seconds. How many tickets can it print in 1 minute?
questions.e: 1 minute = 60 seconds, and 60 / 2 = 30 tickets.

questions.q: We should press the keys ______, not hard.
questions.e: Pressing the keys gently keeps the keyboard safe.

questions.q: Meera's cat likes to sit on the computer. Pets should be kept ______ from the computer.
questions.e: Pets can drop hair on the computer or knock it over, so we keep them away.

questions.q: Arjun's hands are sticky after eating a laddoo. Before using the computer, he should ______ his hands.
questions.e: Sticky hands make the keys and mouse dirty, so we wash and dry our hands first.

questions.q: Rain is coming in through the window near the computer. Arjun should ______ the window.
questions.e: Water can spoil a computer, so we keep it away from rain.

questions.q: Meera's computer is kept in hot sun near a heater. It should be kept in a ______ place.
questions.e: Too much heat can harm a computer, so we keep it in a cool, dry place.

questions.q: A ______ machine washes our clothes.
questions.e: A washing machine is a machine that helps us wash clothes.

questions.q: A computer is made by ______.
questions.e: A computer is a man-made machine. People make it.

questions.q: A fan is a machine. It gives us ______.
questions.e: Machines help us. A fan gives us air on a hot day.

questions.q: A computer can keep many things in it for a long time. We say it has a good ______.
questions.e: A computer has memory, so it can keep our pictures, songs and work.

questions.q: Riya gives the computer the wrong numbers for a sum. The computer will give a ______ answer.
questions.e: A computer only works with what we give it. Wrong numbers in give a wrong answer out.

questions.q: In Paint, we pick a colour from the ______ group.
questions.e: The Colors group has many colour boxes to choose from.

questions.q: Meera wants to draw a round sun in Paint. Which shape will she pick?
questions.e: The Oval shape draws round shapes like a sun or a ball.

questions.q: Arjun drew a house in Paint. To keep his drawing safe, he clicks ______ in the File menu.
questions.e: Save keeps our drawing in the computer so we can open it again.

questions.q: Riya drew a red apple. Now she wants a green leaf. What must she change before she draws the leaf?
questions.e: We choose a new colour from the Colors group before drawing in that colour.

questions.q: Arjun used Fill with Color on a circle, but the colour spread over the whole page. The circle must have a ______ in its line.
questions.e: Fill with Color fills only a closed shape. If the line has a gap, the colour spreads out.

questions.q: Meera types her name on the keyboard. Her name comes on the ______.
questions.e: The monitor shows what we type.

questions.q: Which part of the computer has the power button and many wires going into its back?
questions.e: The CPU box has the power button. The monitor, keyboard and mouse are joined to it with wires.

questions.q: The speakers of Arjun's computer are not working. He can see a cartoon, but he cannot ______ it.
questions.e: Speakers give out sound. Without them we can still see the picture on the monitor.

questions.q: Arjun takes a photo of his birthday cake with a ______.
questions.e: Smartphones, tablets and cameras can take photos.

questions.q: A ______ oven warms our food and beeps when it is done.
questions.e: A microwave oven has a small computer inside that sets the time and beeps.

questions.q: A smartphone is like a small ______ that we can keep in a pocket.
questions.e: A smartphone can do many things a computer does, like games, photos and videos.

questions.q: A robot ______ cleaner moves around and cleans the floor by itself.
questions.e: A robot vacuum cleaner is a smart device that cleans the floor on its own.

questions.q: Riya's smartwatch has stopped working. Its battery needs to be ______.
questions.e: Smart devices need electricity. We charge their battery when it runs out.

questions.q: When the computer is on, a small ______ glows on the CPU.
questions.e: A small light on the CPU box shows that the computer is on.

questions.q: Riya has switched on the computer. She should ______ until the desktop comes.
questions.e: A computer takes a little time to start, so we wait for the desktop.

questions.q: Arjun pressed the power button, but nothing happened. The main switch on the wall was ______.
questions.e: The computer gets electricity only when the main switch is on.

questions.q: Meera has shut down the computer. Now the monitor screen looks ______.
questions.e: After the computer shuts down, nothing is shown, so the screen goes dark.

questions.q: Riya wants to type her age, 6. She presses a ______ key.
questions.e: Number keys are used to type numbers like 6.

questions.q: How many letter keys does Arjun press to type the word 'bat'?
questions.e: The word 'bat' has 3 letters: b, a and t.

questions.q: Meera wants to move the cursor to the line above. Which arrow key should she press?
questions.e: The up arrow key moves the cursor up by one line.

questions.q: Riya types 'sun moon' with one gap. How many keys does she press in all?
questions.e: sun has 3 letters, the gap is 1 space bar, moon has 4 letters: 3 + 1 + 4 = 8.

questions.q: When we move the mouse, the arrow on the screen also ______.
questions.e: The arrow on the screen moves the same way as the mouse.

questions.q: Our first finger rests on the left button of the mouse. Our ______ finger rests on the right button.
questions.e: We keep the first finger on the left button and the middle finger on the right button.

questions.q: To open a picture, Meera clicks two times quickly. Arjun clicks once, waits, and clicks again. Whose way opens the picture?
questions.e: A double click must be two quick clicks. If we wait between them, it is two single clicks.

questions.q: Arjun does one click and then one double click. How many times does he press the left button in all?
questions.e: One click is 1 press and a double click is 2 presses: 1 + 2 = 3.

questions.q: Arjun's teacher shows a video of a tiger in class on a ______.
questions.e: Teachers use computers to show videos and pictures in class.

questions.q: Meera's grandfather reads the ______ on the computer every morning.
questions.e: We can read the news on a computer.

questions.q: At the library, a computer keeps a list of the ______ we take home.
questions.e: Librarians use computers to keep a record of the books we borrow.

questions.q: Riya wants to see how many days are left for her birthday. She can look at the ______ on the computer.
questions.e: A computer has a calendar that shows days, dates and months.

questions.q: Arjun has 3 toy cars and gets 4 more. He adds them on the computer's calculator. What answer does it show?
questions.e: 3 + 4 = 7. A computer can do sums quickly with its calculator.

questions.q: Good manners that we should follow while using the internet are called ______.
questions.e: Netiquette means being polite and respectful online, for example not typing in capital letters to shout.

questions.q: Copying and sharing software, films or music without the owner's permission is called ______.
questions.e: Piracy is illegal; we should use only genuine software and media.

questions.q: Keeping an extra copy of important files on another device, so that they are not lost, is called taking a ______.
questions.e: A backup on a pen drive or another disk lets us get our files back if the computer is damaged or attacked by a virus.

questions.q: Kabir's friend asks for his online game password to 'help him win'. What should Kabir do?
questions.a: Refuse and keep the password secret
o: Write it on the classroom board
Change it to his own name
questions.e: A password must never be shared, even with friends; anyone who knows it can use or misuse the account.

questions.q: Meera sees that a classmate is being sent mean messages in a group chat. What should she do first?
questions.a: Tell a trusted adult and do not forward the messages
o: Join in so she is not targeted
questions.e: Cyberbullying should be reported to a parent or teacher; forwarding or replying only spreads the hurt.

questions.q: Riya gets 4 emails: (A) from her teacher about homework, (B) 'You won Rs 1 lakh, send your OTP', (C) from her cousin with a birthday photo, (D) 'Your account is locked, type your password here'. How many of these are likely phishing emails?
questions.e: B and D try to trick her into giving secret details (OTP and password), so 2 emails are phishing; A and C are from people she knows.

questions.q: Hardware such as a printer or scanner that is connected to the computer from outside is called a ______ device.
questions.e: Peripheral devices are attached to the computer to add input, output or storage.

questions.q: Antivirus is an example of ______ software, which helps to keep the computer healthy.
questions.e: Utility software, such as antivirus and disk cleaners, helps to look after and protect the computer.

questions.q: The speed of a computer's processor (CPU) is measured in ______.
questions.e: Processor speed is measured in hertz, usually gigahertz (GHz); gigabytes measure storage.

questions.q: Putting a program on a computer is called installing it. Removing it from the computer is called ______ it.
questions.e: Uninstalling removes a program and its files so that it no longer runs on the computer.

questions.q: Riya types 25 + 17 on the keyboard. The computer works out 42 and shows it on the monitor. In which stage of the Input-Process-Output cycle is 42 worked out?
questions.e: Typing is input, working out the answer inside the CPU is processing, and showing 42 on the monitor is output.

questions.q: Arjun's computer has Windows, MS Word and Scratch. If Windows is removed, which of the other two programs will still run?
questions.e: Application software needs an operating system to run, so without Windows neither program can work.

questions.q: On Ishaan's computer, Windows, the keyboard and the mouse all work, but the computer says MS Word is not installed. Which type of software is missing?
questions.e: Windows (system software) and the hardware are working; MS Word is application software, so that is what must be installed.

questions.q: Which output device is worn over the ears so that only one person can hear the sound?
questions.e: Headphones give sound output privately; a microphone takes sound as input.

questions.q: Which pen-shaped input device is used to draw or write directly on a screen?
questions.e: A light pen or stylus lets us point, draw and write on the screen like a pen on paper.

questions.q: Which input device do banks use to read the special numbers printed in magnetic ink at the bottom of cheques?
questions.a: MICR|MICR reader|magnetic ink character reader|magnetic ink character recognition
questions.e: MICR (Magnetic Ink Character Recognition) reads the cheque number and bank code quickly and correctly.

questions.q: Kabir's printer prints 12 pages in one minute. How many minutes will it take to print 60 pages?
questions.e: Time = pages to print / pages per minute = 60 / 12 = 5 minutes.

questions.q: A monitor's picture is made of tiny dots called pixels. A small screen has 80 pixels in each row and 60 rows. How many pixels does it have?
questions.e: Total pixels = pixels in a row x number of rows = 80 x 60 = 4800.

questions.q: A few lines, such as your name and class, that are added at the end of every email you send are called your email ______.
questions.e: An email signature is set once and then added automatically to the end of each email.

questions.q: Sending an email that you have received on to another person is called ______ it.
questions.e: Forward sends a received email to someone new; Reply answers the person who sent it.

questions.q: Riya's teacher sends her an email with copies to 3 classmates in CC. Riya wants her answer to reach the teacher and all 3 classmates. Which option should she click?
questions.e: Reply sends the answer only to the sender; Reply All sends it to the sender and everyone in To and CC.

questions.q: An email is sent with 2 addresses in To, 3 in CC and 4 in BCC. How many of these addresses are hidden from the other receivers?
questions.e: Only BCC (Blind Carbon Copy) addresses are hidden, so 4 addresses are hidden; the 5 addresses in To and CC can be seen by everyone.

questions.q: The first slide of a presentation, which usually shows its topic and the presenter's name, is called the ______ slide.
questions.e: The title slide introduces the presentation; the slides after it hold the main content.

questions.q: In which view of PowerPoint does each slide fill the whole screen for the audience?
questions.e: Slide Show view shows slides full screen one by one; Normal view is used to make and edit them.

questions.q: Arjun's presentation has 5 slides. He makes 2 duplicate copies of slide 2 and then deletes slide 4. How many slides are there now?
questions.e: 5 + 2 = 7 slides after duplicating, and 7 - 1 = 6 slides after deleting one.

questions.q: Meera's slide has a lot of text in very small letters, and the class at the back cannot read it. What is the best way to fix the slide?
questions.a: Use fewer words and a bigger font
o: Add more text to explain it
Use light yellow text on a white background
questions.e: Good slides have short points in a large, clear font with colours that stand out from the background.

questions.q: In MS Word, a red wavy line under a word shows a possible ______ mistake.
questions.e: Word underlines words it does not recognise with a red wavy line so that we can check their spelling.

questions.q: The blank space between the text and the edge of the page is called the ______.
questions.e: Every page has top, bottom, left and right margins; text is typed inside them.

questions.q: Arjun wants to write 5 steps of an experiment as a list marked 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5. Which feature should he use?
questions.e: Numbering marks each item with a number in order; Bullets marks items with dots or symbols.

questions.q: Riya presses Ctrl+A and then Ctrl+B in her two-page essay. What happens?
o: Only the first word becomes bold
questions.e: Ctrl+A selects all the text, and Ctrl+B makes the selected text bold.

questions.q: A storage device with no moving parts that works faster than a hard disk is called an ______.
questions.a: SSD|solid state drive|solid-state drive|solid state disk
questions.e: An SSD (Solid State Drive) stores data on memory chips, so it has no spinning disk and is faster.

questions.q: Arjun's pen drive can hold 8 GB. He has already used 6 GB. How many MB of space are left? (1 GB = 1024 MB)
questions.e: Free space = 8 - 6 = 2 GB, and 2 x 1024 = 2048 MB.

questions.q: A 2 GB memory card is used for photos of 512 KB each. How many photos can it hold? (1 GB = 1024 MB, 1 MB = 1024 KB)
The Windows program used to see, open and organise our files and folders is called File ______.
questions.e: File Explorer shows the drives, folders and files on the computer.

questions.q: Which shortcut key is used to switch between open windows in Windows?
questions.e: Holding Alt and pressing Tab moves from one open window to the next.

questions.q: Riya wants to open her 'Project' folder quickly from the desktop, without moving the folder. What should she make on the desktop?
questions.e: A shortcut is a link that opens the real folder; the folder stays where it was saved.

questions.q: A folder named 'Photos' has 3 folders inside it, and each of these folders has 5 files. How many files are inside 'Photos' in all?
questions.e: 3 folders x 5 files = 15 files.

questions.q: In Scratch, the green flag starts a project. Which red button stops all the scripts?
questions.e: The red Stop button, next to the green flag above the stage, stops every running script.

questions.q: In a program, a block such as 'repeat 10' that runs the same steps again and again is called a ______.
questions.e: A loop repeats a set of steps, so we do not have to write the same blocks many times.

questions.q: Algorithm: Step 1 Start. Step 2 Set N = 1. Step 3 Repeat 4 times: N = N x 2. Step 4 Print N. Step 5 Stop. What is printed?
questions.e: N doubles four times: 1 to 2, 4, 8 and then 16.

questions.q: Typing a whole online message in CAPITAL LETTERS is like ______ at the other person.
questions.e: Messages in all capital letters seem loud and rude, so we use normal letters online.

questions.q: Before using a new game or app, Riya should check that it is suitable for her ______.
questions.e: Many games and apps are made for older users; an adult can help check that they suit your age.

questions.q: Riya posts a photo online and deletes it one minute later. Could someone have saved a copy already? (yes/no)
questions.e: Once something is posted, others can copy or save it quickly, so think before you post.

questions.q: A simple colouring game on Meera's tablet asks: 'Allow this app to know your location?' What should she choose?
o: Allow and share it with friends
questions.e: A colouring game does not need to know where you are, so do not give it your location.

questions.q: Arjun's password is 'arjun2016', which is his name and the year he was born. Why is this a weak password?
questions.e: Names and birth years are known to many people, so such a password is easy to guess; mix letters, numbers and symbols instead.

questions.q: Is a keyboard hardware or software?
questions.e: A keyboard is a physical part that we can touch, so it is hardware.

questions.q: People who write the programs that make up software are called ______.
questions.e: Programmers write instructions (programs) that tell the computer what to do.

questions.q: During a power cut, Riya's computer stays on for a few minutes so she can save her work. Which device is helping her?
questions.e: A UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) has a battery that gives power for a short time during a power cut.

questions.q: Aman's mouse fell off the table and stopped working. Was hardware or software damaged?
questions.e: The mouse is a physical part, so it is hardware; software cannot be dropped or broken like this.

questions.q: Which pair has one piece of hardware and one piece of software?
questions.e: A printer can be touched, so it is hardware; MS Word is a program, so it is software.

questions.q: Meera's computer has a monitor, keyboard, mouse and CPU, but she cannot draw on it because no drawing program is installed. What does her computer need?
questions.a: software|drawing software|application software|a drawing program|drawing program
questions.e: Hardware cannot do a task on its own; it needs software, such as a drawing program, to tell it what to do.

questions.q: In some offices, workers put a finger on a small device to mark that they have come to work. This input device is a ______ scanner.
questions.e: A fingerprint (biometric) scanner reads the lines of a finger to identify a person.

questions.q: On a laptop, the flat pad on which you move your finger to move the pointer is called a ______.
questions.e: A touchpad does the work of a mouse on a laptop.

questions.q: In an online class, Aman hears his teacher through his computer's speakers. For Aman's computer, are the speakers an input or an output device?
questions.e: Speakers give out sound from the computer, so they are output devices.

questions.q: Meera uses a mouse, a printer, a microphone and a speaker. Which two of these are input devices?
questions.e: The mouse and microphone send information into the computer; the printer and speaker give output.

questions.q: The short line in an email that tells what the email is about is called the ______.
questions.e: The subject line helps the receiver know what the email is about before opening it.

questions.q: Riya types www.ncert.nic.in in the long box at the top of her web browser. This box is called the ______ bar.
questions.e: The address bar is where we type a website's address (URL) to open it.

questions.q: Aman got an email from Meera and wants to answer her. Which button should he click?
questions.e: Reply sends an answer to the person who sent the email.

questions.q: Aman wants to check that his email to his teacher has really gone. In which folder should he look?
questions.e: Emails that have been sent are kept in the Sent folder.

questions.q: Aman sends an email to Riya and puts Meera and Rohan in the CC box. How many people receive the email?
questions.e: Riya gets it from the To box and Meera and Rohan get copies: 1 + 2 = 3 people.

questions.q: In MS Paint, which shape is used to draw a box with sharp corners?
questions.e: The Rectangle shape draws boxes; holding Shift with it draws a square.

questions.q: In MS Paint, which brush sprays tiny dots, like a spray can?
questions.e: The Airbrush scatters small dots of colour, like paint from a spray can.

questions.q: In MS Paint, which tool is used to mark a part of the picture so that it can be moved or copied?
questions.e: The Select tool marks an area of the picture; then it can be moved, copied or cut.

questions.q: Meera drew one flower in Paint and wants four more flowers exactly like it. After selecting it, what should she do?
questions.e: Copy keeps the flower and paste adds another copy each time, so she can make as many as she needs.

questions.q: Rohan's drawing of a car faces left. He wants a mirror image that faces right. Which option should he use?
questions.e: Flip horizontal turns the picture left to right like a mirror image.

questions.q: Arjun drew a circle with a small gap in its outline. He used Fill with colour inside it. What happens?
questions.a: The colour spills out of the circle
o: Only the inside of the circle is filled
questions.e: Fill with colour works only inside a closed shape; through the gap, the colour spreads to the area outside too.

questions.q: In MS Word, the blinking line that shows where the next letter will appear is called the ______.
questions.e: The cursor (insertion point) blinks to show where the text will be typed.

questions.q: Which shortcut key is used to print a document in MS Word?
questions.e: Ctrl+P opens the Print option so the document can be printed on paper.

questions.q: Riya cut a sentence with Ctrl+X and clicked where she wants it. Which shortcut key will place it there?
questions.e: Ctrl+V pastes the cut or copied text at the cursor; cut and paste moves text.

questions.q: Aman selects his heading 'Our Earth'. He wants it bold and underlined. Which two shortcut keys should he press?
questions.e: Ctrl+B makes text bold and Ctrl+U underlines it; Ctrl+I would make it italic.

questions.q: The small card put into a mobile phone or camera to store photos is called a ______ card.
questions.e: A memory card is a small storage device used in phones and cameras.

questions.q: Which can store more: a 700 MB CD or a 4 GB pen drive? (1 GB = 1024 MB)
questions.a: the pen drive|pen drive|pendrive|4 GB pen drive
questions.e: 4 GB = 4 x 1024 = 4096 MB, which is more than 700 MB, so the pen drive stores more.

questions.q: A file that we type and save in MS Word is called a ______.
questions.e: Files made in a word processor such as MS Word are called documents.

questions.q: Which shortcut key selects all the files in an open folder?
questions.e: Ctrl+A selects all the items, for example all files in a folder or all text in a document.

questions.q: Meera emptied the Recycle Bin. Can she now restore those files from the Recycle Bin? (yes/no)
questions.e: Emptying the Recycle Bin removes the files from it for ever, so they cannot be restored from there.

questions.q: Riya made a folder named 'Class 4' and then a folder named 'Science' inside it. 'Science' is called a ______ of 'Class 4'.
questions.e: A folder kept inside another folder is called a subfolder.

questions.q: Aman has three files: tiger.bmp, poem.docx and race.sb3. Which file did he make in Scratch?
questions.e: The extension tells the file type: .sb3 is Scratch, .bmp is Paint and .docx is Word.

questions.q: In Scratch, what is the x-position of a sprite standing at the exact centre of the stage?
questions.e: The centre of the Scratch stage is x = 0, y = 0.

questions.q: Which Scratch extension adds blocks such as 'pen down', so a sprite draws a line as it moves?
questions.e: The Pen extension lets a sprite draw: after 'pen down', it leaves a line wherever it moves.

questions.q: Rohan's script is: when green flag clicked, forever [move 10 steps, if on edge, bounce]. When will the sprite stop moving?
questions.a: When the red stop sign is clicked
questions.e: A forever block repeats without end; the sprite bounces at the edge and keeps going until the stop sign is clicked.

questions.q: Which stage of the AI project cycle comes straight after data acquisition?
questions.e: After collecting data, we explore it, often with graphs, to find patterns before building a model.

questions.q: Siri, Alexa and Google Assistant are examples of AI-based ______ assistants.
questions.e: These assistants use AI to understand spoken commands and reply in human language.

questions.q: The 4Ws problem canvas used in problem scoping asks Who, What, Where and ______.
questions.e: Who has the problem, What it is, Where it happens and Why solving it matters.

questions.q: Which domain of AI works mainly with numbers and tables of data, for example to predict sales from past records?
questions.e: Data science finds patterns in numerical and tabular data; computer vision uses images and NLP uses language.

questions.q: A smart speaker in a home keeps recording conversations and sends them to a company server without the family knowing. Which AI ethics concern does this mainly raise?
questions.e: Collecting personal data without people knowing or agreeing is a breach of their privacy.

questions.q: A developer writes fixed if-then rules for a chatbot instead of letting it learn from examples. Which type of AI model is this?
questions.a: rule-based|rule based|rule-based model|rule based approach|rule-based approach
questions.e: In a rule-based model, people write the rules; in a learning-based model, the machine learns the rules from data.

questions.q: A model sorts 100 fruit photos as "apple" or "not apple". It correctly says "apple" for 30 apples and "not apple" for 50 other fruits. It wrongly calls 8 other fruits apples and misses 12 apples. What is its accuracy?
questions.e: Correct predictions = 30 + 50 = 80 out of 100, so accuracy = 80/100 x 100 = 80%.

questions.q: What is the full form of BIOS?
questions.a: Basic Input Output System|Basic Input/Output System|Basic Input-Output System
questions.e: The BIOS is firmware that checks the hardware and starts loading the operating system when the computer is switched on.

questions.q: Which type of printer sprays tiny drops of ink onto the paper?
questions.a: inkjet printer|inkjet|ink jet|ink-jet printer|ink jet printer
questions.e: An inkjet printer sprays ink through tiny nozzles; a laser printer uses toner powder instead.

questions.q: What is the speed at which a processor works, measured in gigahertz (GHz), called?
questions.e: A 3 GHz processor has 3 billion clock cycles every second.

questions.q: What are the very small, very fast storage locations inside the CPU that hold the data being processed at that moment called?
questions.e: Registers are inside the CPU itself, so they are even faster than cache memory.

questions.q: Which type of computer, such as the PARAM series built in India, is used for huge scientific calculations like weather forecasting?
questions.e: Supercomputers are the fastest computers; PARAM supercomputers are built by C-DAC in India.

questions.q: A library wants to turn old printed books into text that can be edited and searched on a computer. After scanning the pages, which technology should it use?
questions.e: OCR recognises the printed letters in a scanned image and turns them into editable text.

questions.q: Neha downloads a photo editor that she can use free for 30 days, after which she must pay to keep using it. What kind of software is this?
questions.e: Shareware is given free for a trial period; freeware stays free for ever.

questions.q: A computer lab has these devices: scanner, monitor, printer, speaker, keyboard and microphone. How many of them are output devices?
questions.e: The monitor, printer and speaker give output; the scanner, keyboard and microphone are input devices.

questions.q: What is the small text file that a website stores in your browser to remember you, such as the items in your shopping cart?
questions.e: Cookies help websites remember you, but they can also be used to track what you do online.

questions.q: Criminals fix a hidden device on the card slot of an ATM to copy the details of every card put into it. What is this fraud called?
questions.e: A skimmer copies card details; covering the keypad and checking the card slot help to stay safe.

questions.q: What is the general name for crimes carried out using computers and the internet, such as hacking and online fraud?
questions.e: In India, cybercrimes are dealt with under the Information Technology Act, 2000.

questions.q: An attacker floods a school website with so many fake requests that genuine students cannot open it. What is this type of attack called?
questions.a: denial of service|DoS|denial-of-service|DoS attack|DDoS|distributed denial of service
questions.e: A denial of service attack overloads a server so that it cannot serve real users.

questions.q: While Meena types her PIN at an ATM, a man standing behind her secretly watches her fingers to learn it. What is this trick called?
questions.e: Shoulder surfing is stealing information by watching someone; cover the keypad when you type a PIN.

questions.q: Aman changes his phone lock from a 4-digit PIN to a 6-digit PIN. Each digit can be any of 0 to 9. How many times as many possible PINs does the new lock have?
questions.e: 4 digits give 10 x 10 x 10 x 10 = 10000 PINs and 6 digits give 1000000, and 1000000 / 10000 = 100, so a longer PIN is much harder to guess.

questions.q: Who invented the World Wide Web?
questions.e: Tim Berners-Lee created the World Wide Web in 1989 while working at CERN.

questions.q: Buying and selling goods and services over the internet is called ______.
questions.e: Online shopping websites are examples of e-commerce.

questions.q: What is a website or web page on which a person regularly posts articles or diary-like entries, usually with the newest shown first?
questions.e: Blog is short for weblog; the person who writes it is a blogger.

questions.q: Which internet service lets several people in different places see and talk to one another live, as in an online class?
questions.e: Video conferencing sends live sound and video between people over the internet.

questions.q: The students of a class build a shared website on which any of them can add new pages about their town or edit pages written by others. What kind of website is this?
questions.e: A wiki, such as Wikipedia, lets many users write and edit its content together.

questions.q: Ramesh pays his electricity bill, files his income tax return and applies for a passport online through government websites. What is the use of the internet to deliver government services called?
questions.e: E-governance means providing government services to citizens online.

questions.q: A home internet connection has a speed of 80 Mbps (megabits per second). How many seconds will it take to download a 750 MB (megabyte) game? (8 bits = 1 byte)
questions.e: 80 megabits per second / 8 = 10 megabytes per second, and 750 / 10 = 75 seconds.

questions.q: What is the full form of HDD?
questions.e: A hard disk drive stores data magnetically on spinning metal platters.

questions.q: Which type of ROM can be erased by shining ultraviolet light on it and then reprogrammed?
questions.a: EPROM|erasable programmable read only memory|erasable programmable ROM
questions.e: EPROM is erased with UV light; EEPROM is erased electrically.

questions.q: Which of these optical discs can store the most data?
questions.e: A CD holds the least, a DVD more, and a Blu-ray disc the most, as it uses a blue-violet laser.

questions.q: Ravi opens so many programs that the RAM becomes full, so the operating system uses part of the hard disk as if it were extra RAM. What is this called?
questions.e: Virtual memory lets the computer run more programs than the RAM can hold, but it is slower than real RAM.

questions.q: A picture is 800 pixels wide and 600 pixels high, and each pixel takes 3 bytes. What is the size of the picture in bytes?
A 1 TB hard disk already holds 424 GB of data. How many 4 GB movies can still be saved on it? (1 TB = 1024 GB)
questions.e: Free space = 1024 - 424 = 600 GB, and 600 / 4 = 150 movies.

questions.q: What is the full form of NIC?
questions.e: A NIC is the card or chip that connects a computer to a network.

questions.q: Which type of cable, made of pairs of copper wires twisted together, is commonly used in LANs?
questions.a: twisted pair|twisted pair cable|twisted-pair|twisted-pair cable|UTP|Ethernet cable
questions.e: Twisting the wires in pairs reduces interference; these cables connect computers to switches.

questions.q: What is the unique hardware address, fixed on every network interface card by its maker, called?
questions.a: MAC address|MAC|media access control address|physical address
questions.e: A MAC address, such as 00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E, is fixed on the card, while an IP address can change.

questions.q: Which cable has a central copper wire surrounded by insulation and a metal mesh shield, and is commonly used for cable TV?
questions.e: The metal shield of a coaxial cable protects the signal from outside interference.

questions.q: When a photo is sent over a network, it is broken into small units that may travel by different routes and are put back together at the destination. What are these units called?
questions.e: Splitting data into packets lets many users share the network and lets lost pieces be sent again.

questions.q: An IPv4 address, such as 192.168.1.5, has four numbers separated by dots, and each number is stored in 8 bits. What is the largest value any one of these numbers can have?
questions.e: The largest 8-bit number is 11111111 = 255, so an address such as 192.168.1.300 is not valid.

questions.q: Convert binary 1110011 to octal.
questions.e: Group in threes from the right: 1 | 110 | 011 = 1, 6, 3, so the octal number is 163.

questions.q: Which shortcut key saves the document you are working on?
questions.e: Ctrl+S saves; save often so that work is not lost if the power goes off.

questions.q: In a spreadsheet program, what is a file that contains one or more worksheets called?
questions.e: A spreadsheet file is a workbook, and each sheet inside it is a worksheet.

questions.q: Which part of a page in a word processor shows text, such as page numbers, at the bottom of every page?
questions.e: The header is at the top of every page and the footer is at the bottom.

questions.q: Which word processor feature records every edit made to a document, so that each change can later be accepted or rejected?
questions.e: Track Changes shows who changed what, which is useful when several people edit one document.

questions.q: A teacher has a spreadsheet of 40 students and wants to see only the rows of students who scored more than 80, without deleting the others. Which feature should she use?
questions.e: A filter hides the rows that do not meet the condition; removing the filter shows them again.

questions.q: Riya wants a chart that shows what share of her pocket money she spends on food, books, travel and savings. Which type of chart is most suitable?
questions.e: A pie chart shows how each part makes up a whole, as slices of a circle.

questions.q: The marks 45, 78, 62 and 90 are sorted in descending order. Which mark is now in the third position?
questions.e: Descending order is largest first: 90, 78, 62, 45, so the third mark is 62.

questions.q: Cell D2 contains the formula =$B2*C$1. It is copied to cell E3. What formula appears in E3?
questions.e: Moving one column right and one row down: $B2 keeps column B but the row becomes 3; C$1 keeps row 1 but the column becomes D.

questions.q: Which symbol must be written at the end of an if statement line in Python?
questions.e: For example: if x > 5: - the colon starts the indented block.

questions.q:

x = 4
if x > 2 and x < 4:
    print("Yes")
else:
    print("No")
questions.e: x > 2 is True but x < 4 is False, and and needs both to be True, so the else part runs.

questions.q:
What is the output?
age = 16
if age >= 18:
    print("Adult")
else:
    if age >= 13:
        print("Teen")
    else:
        print("Child")
questions.e: 16 is not >= 18, so the else block runs; inside it 16 >= 13 is True, so Teen is printed.

questions.q:
What is the output?
n = 0
if n:
    print("Non-zero")
else:
    print("Zero")
questions.e: Python treats the number 0 as False in a condition, so the else part runs.

questions.q:
What is the output?
year = 1900
if (year % 4 == 0 and year % 100 != 0) or year % 400 == 0:
    print("Leap")
else:
    print("Not leap")
questions.e: 1900 is divisible by 4 and by 100, so the first part is False, and 1900 % 400 is 300, so the whole condition is False.

questions.q: What is the data type of "25" (written with quotation marks) in Python?
questions.e: Anything inside quotation marks is a string, even if it looks like a number.

questions.q: What are the only two values of the bool data type in Python?
questions.a: True and False|True False|False and True|True, False|True or False
questions.e: bool values are written True and False, with a capital first letter.

questions.q: Which Python function converts the number 45 into the string "45"?
questions.e: str(45) gives "45"; int() and float() convert the other way, into numbers.

questions.q: What is the data type of the result of 7 / 7 in Python?
questions.e: The / operator always gives a float, so 7 / 7 is 1.0, not 1.

questions.q:
What is the output?
print(str(10) + str(5))
questions.e: str() turns both numbers into strings, and + joins strings, giving "105".

questions.q:
What is the output?
print(10 // 4.0)
questions.e: 10 // 4.0 is floor division, giving the whole-number part 2, but because 4.0 is a float the result is a float: 2.0.

questions.q: Which Python loop keeps repeating as long as its condition is True?
questions.e: A while loop checks its condition before each repetition and stops when it becomes False.

questions.q:
How many times is Hi printed?
for i in range(5, 0, -1):
    print("Hi")
questions.e: range(5, 0, -1) gives 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, which is 5 values.

questions.q:
What is the output?
for i in range(1, 6):
    if i == 3:
        continue
    print(i, end=" ")
questions.e: continue skips the print only when i is 3; the loop then goes on with 4 and 5.

questions.q:
What is the output?
x = 10
while x > 1:
    x = x // 2
    print(x, end=" ")
questions.e: x becomes 10 // 2 = 5, then 5 // 2 = 2, then 2 // 2 = 1; now x > 1 is False, so the loop stops.

questions.q: Which Python operator does floor division, giving the whole-number part of a division?
questions.e: 7 // 2 gives 3, while 7 / 2 gives 3.5.

questions.q: Which logical operator gives True only when both conditions are True?
questions.e: For example, 5 > 2 and 3 > 1 is True, but 5 > 2 and 3 > 8 is False.

questions.q: What is the output of: print(5 > 3 or 2 > 9)
questions.e: or gives True if at least one condition is True, and 5 > 3 is True.

questions.q:
What is the output?
x = 10
x += 5
x *= 2
print(x)
questions.e: x += 5 makes x 15, and x *= 2 makes it 30.

questions.q:
What is the output?
print(17 % 3 ** 2)
questions.e: ** comes before %, so 3 ** 2 = 9, and 17 % 9 = 8.

questions.q:
What is the output?
print(10 - 4 / 2 * 3 + 2 ** 2)
questions.e: 2 ** 2 = 4, then 4 / 2 = 2.0 and 2.0 x 3 = 6.0, so 10 - 6.0 + 4 = 8.0; / makes the result a float.
